Braver and stronger – Mansell lays down challenge as Burgess Hill Town seek league turn-around

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • So says boss Gary Mansell after the Hillians let a 2-1 lead slip at Stanway Rovers on Saturday to make it three points from the past 18 available.
  • Harry Lawson and MoM George Vorster put Hill 1-0 and 2-1 up in Essex but despite the second coming with only 15 minutes left, Mansell’s men conceded with eight to go.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

So says boss Gary Mansell after the Hillians let a 2-1 lead slip at Stanway Rovers on Saturday to make it three points from the past 18 available.

Harry Lawson and MoM George Vorster put Hill 1-0 and 2-1 up in Essex but despite the second coming with only 15 minutes left, Mansell’s men conceded with eight to go.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

They should be lifted for the league campaign by Tuesday night’s 6-1 Velocity Trophy win at Crowborough, with Jack Strange, Yoan Edoukou, George Vorster (2) and Shamir Fenelon (2) scoring.

Mansell was asked after the Stanway draw how he felt and remarked: “The same as after the last few games with this little run that we’re in.

According to recent reports, "We just can’t get over the line. We can’t fault the boys’ effort and work-rate, which was superb. In the second half we were on the front foot again.

Recent findings suggest that "But we’re a little nervous going the other way at times – particularly when we’re in front. And ultimately, that mindset is not helping us.

"When we go 2-1 up we stop doing what we were doing. People think the right thing to do is to drop deep and tighten up. But all you do is invite pressure into areas where you then give away a cheap free-kick and you get punished.

"We need to be mentally stronger and control a game better by staying brave in possession and keeping the ball, which doesn’t allow them to have the ball. It’s all about playing the game in their half rather than our half.”.

Mansell does not think Hill were a long way off becoming a winning team again.

Recent findings suggest that "We’re struggling to get over the line because of nervousness around the group. This is a situation we haven’t been in for the three years I’ve been at the club,” he added.

"All the games have been tight other than the Enfield game. I don’t think we’re a million miles away. We’re drawing games that could go either way. We just need to get one over the line to kick-start something.”.

Recent findings suggest that mansell thanked fans for continuing to turn up in good numbers. “It was a good turnout (at Stanway) considering how far we were from home. We do appreciate the support away from home.

"Stick with us, we’ll turn it round and get some wins and we will be smiling again.”.

They host in-form Eastbourne Borough on Saturday.

Mansell mentioned: “We’re not going to shy away from anything. We’ll keep plugging away trying to win games. We’ll go into Saturday as positive as we can.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Matt Law | 25 Nov 2026 19:55, Last updated: 25 Nov 2026 19:57.
  • Anthony Gordon created Champions League history in Barcelona's 4-1 success over Sabah in the league stage of the competition on Wednesday night.
  • The England international scored twice in Azerbaijan to play a leading role in Hansi Flick's side securing an impressive win in the European Cup.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Matt Law | 25 Nov 2026 19:55, Last updated: 25 Nov 2026 19:57.

Anthony Gordon created Champions League history in Barcelona's 4-1 success over Sabah in the league stage of the competition on Wednesday night.

The England international scored twice in Azerbaijan to play a leading role in Hansi Flick's side securing an impressive win in the European Cup.

Gordon has now scored six Champions League goals in Azerbaijan, which is the most any English player has netted in away games in one country in the tournament.

Four of the attacker's goals in Azerbaijan came against Qarabag during his time with Newcastle United, before scoring twice more against Sabah.

Sources indicate that 6 - Anthony Gordon's six UEFA Champions League goals in Azerbaijan are the most any English player has scored in away games in one country in the competition. Tourist. https://t.co/7OfdYkdzch.

The 25-year-old is now on five goals and five assists in 17 appearances for Barcelona since his arrival at the club from Newcastle.

Meanwhile, Gordon's overall record in the Champions League is 13 goals and two assists in 23 appearances in the tournament.

Barcelona have now picked up 12 points from their five matches in the league stage of the Champions League, which has left them in fourth spot in the overall table.

Flick's team were missing Lamine Yamal on Wednesday due to a slight ankle injury; in his absence, Karim Adeyemi and Gabriel Jesus were also on the scoresheet.

Barcelona will be aiming to make it six straight wins in all competitions when they continue their La Liga campaign against Deportivo La Coruna on Sunday afternoon.

The Catalan outfit will then welcome Atletico Madrid to Camp Nou in their first match of December, before facing Celta Vigo in their third league game in quick succession.

Barcelona's next Champions League game is at home to Manchester City on December 8.

The Blues were thumped in their home cup clash with higher-division Broadbridge Heath nine days ago but responded with a 2-0 SCFL Premier win at Roffey thanks to Josh Wright’s double.

Recent findings suggest that boss Green said: “It was a very important win. They’re up there and competing so it was similar to the East Grinstead game – it’s nice to get the wins against the teams up there with you.

According to recent reports, "It was a cagey game, first half. First 20 minutes I thought they were the better team without really creating any chances.

"We slowly grew into the game and scored our first through Josh and we were pleased to go in 1-0 up at half-time after what was probably a 50/50 half.

"Second half I thought we went up a gear, I can’t really remember Roffey having a chance of note in the second half.

"The most important things were three points and another clean sheet – I think it was deserved over the 90 minutes.”.

Green noted of the cup loss: "Broadbridge Heath are a good side but we made it way too easy for them, which is very unlike us. We said to the boys ‘you’ve got to bounce back’ – and on Saturday they did.”.

From joy to frustration in Worthing’s week of extremes

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Boss Adam Hinshelwood was as frustrated in midweek as he had been pleased at the weekend – and is demanding more consistency from his players, particularly in their defending.
  • Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that the high was Jordan Young’s double clinching Saturday’s 2-1 Woodside Road win over second-placed Harrogate. The low was letting in three in four minutes to scupper their hopes of a result at Woking on Tuesday night.

Boss Adam Hinshelwood was as frustrated in midweek as he had been pleased at the weekend – and is demanding more consistency from his players, particularly in their defending.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

After Saturday’s win, Hinshelwood noted the display showed his squad were learning as they went.

It has been revealed that he remarked: “It was probably one of our best wins if you look at where Harrogate are in the league and that we’d come off the back of that late goal conceded at Scunthorpe the previous week. We wanted a response to that and got it.

“They probably shaded the first half but we scored at a good time – in fact Jordan scored twice at good times.

Industry observers note that “At 1-1 we had a real go and highlights how far we have come. Settling for a draw just isn’t in our mindset. We’ve had a few games that could have gone either way but we will always try to win games.

“The second goal came from the type of move we’ve been working on in training.”.

It has been revealed that hinshelwood is delighted by Young’s influence on the campaign. He signed from Torquay in September after Teddy Jenks left the Reds – and he’s proved the perfect replacement so far.

Industry observers note that “He’s a top talent who we’d chased for a while. He’d done it against us too many times and we knew what he could do for us.”.

Young has scored six goals in 15 appearances and Hinshelwood remarked: “He is scoring, assisting and creating.”.

But Tuesday’s loss at Woking – where goals by Ashley Nathaniel-George and Dominic Johnson-Fisher (2) proved in vain – left Hinshelwood hugely frustrated.

“We’re gifting games to our opponents. They don’t have to do anything to beat us. We scored two unbelievable goals but gifted them goals – and it’s a common trend,” he told club media.

“Good teams are consistent week after week but we have turned up and just thought we can do enough to win. At this level you get found out.

Recent findings suggest that “We have no-one to blame but ourselves. Three goals in four minutes – it’s nowhere near good enough. We’ve got to find a way to defend our box on a consistent basis.”.

The seventh-placed Rebels go to Altrincham on Saturday then visit Wick next Tuesday in the Sussex Senior Cup third round.

Breaking: Gary Neville tears into Man United's Matthijs de Ligt for 'unforgivable' defending that led to Leny Yoro's red card - and claims duo played like 'they have never had basic defensive training'

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (789 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 12:23 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 10:28 EST, 24 November 2026.
  • Gary Neville led the criticism of Manchester United's defending in the opening minutes against Liverpool as Mauricio Pochettino's reign started in disastrous fashion at Anfield.
  • After just eight minutes, his prepares were thrown into tatters when errors from Matthijs de Ligt and Leny Yoro saw the latter sent off before Liverpool took a swift lead.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By LEWIS BROWNING, SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 12:23 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 10:28 EST, 24 November 2026.

Gary Neville led the criticism of Manchester United's defending in the opening minutes against Liverpool as Mauricio Pochettino's reign started in disastrous fashion at Anfield.

After just eight minutes, his prepares were thrown into tatters when errors from Matthijs de Ligt and Leny Yoro saw the latter sent off before Liverpool took a swift lead.

A long ball from Ronald Araujo should have been dealt with easily by De Ligt, but the Dutchman found himself in no man's land, left the ball, and Alexander Isak raced clear.

That left Yoro scrambling to try to recover the situation for his side, but Isak stepped across him and he ended up fouling the Reds forward.

Referee Sam Barrott wasted no time in pulling out the red card, and United found themselves reduced to 10 men just minutes into a vital clash.

And former United defender Neville didn't hold back when it came to his analysis as he tore into the two players at fault.

Sources indicate that leny Yoro is SENT OFF after eight minutes! 😱 pic.twitter.com/VKYvckvBBP.

Gary Neville torn into Manchester United duo Leny Yoro (right) and Matthijs de Ligt after the former was sent off.

Neville (pictured) questioned why the duo were playing as if they had 'never had basic training of how to play in defence'.

'When I saw De Ligt's name on the team sheet I have to admit I was absolutely stunned,' he said, speaking on Sky Sports. 'And the reason I was stunned was because of this. If you'd watched him in Como four weeks ago he was very much well off it and that is just a basic ball over the top.

Recent findings suggest that 'It's his problem to start with, Yoro can be further across, but De Ligt is miles away from it, then Yoro has to get further round, he reacts late, his anticipation is poor. It's so clumsy from Yoro, he makes a lot of these types of mistakes.

'You could argue Isak delays to make sure Yoro runs into him, but it's naivety.'.

Pochettino was left scrambling to think of ideas to tighten up the defence but, before he could bring Harry Maguire on, it was 2-0 through Florian Wirtz.

Maguire eventually came on but it felt like too little, too late.

It has been revealed that 'We saw him in Como and he has been out for a year,' Neville continued on De Ligt. 'It is really tough to come back. To have him out there in a game like this, he has been exposed. Yoro's positioning is poor, he has to be across, you have to cover your mate. It is bad all around from United.

'Michael Carrick will be watching and say that's what I was having to deal with.'.

In a recent development, and his criticism didn't stop there. After having the chance to re-watch the incident, Neville's criticism grew even stronger.

De Ligt (left) failed to deal with a long ball as Alexander Isak (right) raced away before the foul.

Former United captain Roy Keane (pictured) added that he was 'amazed' by the errors made.

In a recent development, 'It's as bad defending from two centre backs defending a long ball as you will see,' the former defender, who likened a return from a year out to playing after six pints of alcohol, added. 'De Ligt is well out of it - he's been out so I have some sympathy. But between them, to let the ball beat you, it's unforgivable.

According to recent reports, 'It is shocking. Whilst Man United have those types of defenders in their team, they have no chance of keeping a clean sheet.

It has been revealed that 'It's basic understanding of how to play a position. It's the fundamentals. It's like these guys have never had basic training of how to play in defence.'.

Former United captain Roy Keane chimed in too, adding at half-time: 'It doesn't matter if it's a back four or back five, you do the basics right.

'I'm amazed at this level, I know he's been out a while, but it's really poor defending. He's never getting that ball.

'If you're a defender you always expect the worst. Isak's done well and I actually don't think he's going to get the ball.

It has been revealed that 'There's no way he's (Yoro) getting the ball, it's clumsy by United. Straight ball over the top and he's in significant trouble. But there's no way he's getting that ball. I know he's quick and sharp but it's really poor defending. Players not smelling danger.'.

The deal is believed to have an option to buy for around £20m but has so far Promise has struggled to make an impression in Fabian Hurzeler's first team.

David has totalled just 23 minutes of Premier League football without scoring and didn’t make the squad for the defeat at Hull.

"It's getting step by step closer to the demands and the things we ask of him, especially regarding intensity," he explained.

Hurzeler compared David's situation to that of new arrival Femi Azeez, insisting that players outside the starting XI must take responsibility for forcing their way into contention.

"Tobi [Promise] has to use every training session, no matter how long we're on the pitch, to be at his highest level. He needs to do extra work in the gym and extra work after training.

"If you're a non-starter, that's what I demand from the players. You shouldn't be happy with the situation. No player should be happy about being a non-starter and not playing in games.".

Promise arrived at Brighton with an impressive goalscoring record. He scored 41 goals in 82 appearances for Union Saint-Gilloise, helping the Belgian club to their first league title in 90 years.

He also has four goals in 18 appearances for Canada, including a goal at the 2026 World Cup.

Hurzeler believes the responsibility ultimately rests with the player to make the most of his opportunities.

"You need to take ownership and work as hard as possible because that's the only thing you can control," he said to Sussex World.

Sources indicate that "You can complain about the situation, but I've learned one thing in life: complaining never helps. It's about doing the hard work and taking ownership of your own journey and your own process.".

#130475. Jose Mourinho sends clear Real Madrid message to Eder Militao and Antonio Rudiger after PSV double substitution

📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Co ↗ Open Full Page

Jose Mourinho sends clear Real Madrid message to Eder Militao and Antonio Rudiger after PSV double substitution

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (884 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Naim Beneddra | 25 Nov 2026 19:56.
  • Real Madrid manager Jose Mourinho has offered a revealing assessment of his defensive hierarchy after substituting Eder Militao and Antonio Rudiger at half-time during Tuesday's 5-1 Champions League victory over PSV Eindhoven.
  • Los Blancos were trailing 1-0 at the Santiago Bernabeu when Mourinho made three changes at the interval, withdrawing both experienced centre-backs alongside Aurelien Tchouameni.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Naim Beneddra | 25 Nov 2026 19:56.

Real Madrid manager Jose Mourinho has offered a revealing assessment of his defensive hierarchy after substituting Eder Militao and Antonio Rudiger at half-time during Tuesday's 5-1 Champions League victory over PSV Eindhoven.

Los Blancos were trailing 1-0 at the Santiago Bernabeu when Mourinho made three changes at the interval, withdrawing both experienced centre-backs alongside Aurelien Tchouameni. Ibrahima Konate and Dean Huijsen entered in defence, while Jude Bellingham replaced the French midfielder.

The decision preceded a remarkable turnaround. Madrid scored five unanswered goals in the second half, with Bellingham, Federico Valverde, Kylian Mbappe and Vinicius Junior contributing to a victory that maintained their perfect Champions League record after five matches.

Although Mourinho insisted that the improvement was primarily down to a collective change in mentality, his explanation for replacing Militao and Rudiger offered an insight into why Konate and Huijsen have established themselves as his preferred central-defensive partnership.

The Portuguese coach acknowledged that the two younger defenders at the moment benefit from greater match sharpness, while identifying specific qualities that make them particularly valuable to his system.

Speaking to Movistar after the match, Mourinho explained that his decision had been influenced by several factors, including the yellow cards shown to Rudiger and Tchouameni during the opening period.

"A bit of everything," he said when asked whether the substitutions were motivated by fitness, disciplinary concerns or a desire to change the game.

"We had two players on yellow cards in a game against some very quick players, which was a risk.".

However, Mourinho's subsequent assessment was arguably more significant for the two defenders who had been withdrawn.

"Obviously, the two centre-backs who have been playing more regularly are in a better rhythm," he continued.

"Dean is our best player at bringing the ball out from the back, Konate is playing pretty well... and I thought those changes could help us.".

Those comments underline the advantages at the moment enjoyed by Huijsen and Konate, who have become Mourinho's regular pairing since the beginning of the campaign.

Huijsen's ability to progress possession from defence is particularly important in a Madrid side expected to dominate the ball, while Konate provides the physical presence and defensive intensity required when the team presses high.

Both qualities were evident in the second half against PSV, when Madrid pushed their defensive line forward and prevented the Dutch visitors from progressing comfortably through midfield.

Mourinho nevertheless resisted the suggestion that his defensive substitutions alone had transformed the contest.

The former Chelsea and Manchester United manager also credited Bellingham's introduction and a collective improvement in pressing, explaining that his players had struggled to win individual battles before the interval.

"The second half was a question of mentality," Mourinho stated. "We made changes, yes, and Jude is a different kind of player who gives us what we lacked in the first half, but collectively we were better in the second half.".

His explanation makes it difficult to interpret the removal of Militao and Rudiger as an outright rejection of either player. Yet publicly highlighting the superior rhythm and individual qualities of their competitors offers a clear indication of the current pecking order.

The situation is particularly delicate for Rudiger, whose contract expires in June 2027.

The 33-year-old German has found regular opportunities difficult to secure under Mourinho, and reports in Spain have suggested that Real Madrid are increasingly unlikely to offer him another extension.

His experience remains an asset, particularly across a demanding season involving several competitions, but his reduced role raises questions about whether he will remain at the Bernabeu beyond next summer.

Militao faces a different challenge.

The Brazil international remains under contract until June 2028, although his recent career has been disrupted by two serious anterior cruciate ligament injuries and further muscular problems.

He has played only five minutes in La Liga this season, with his Champions League appearances providing most of his opportunities to regain competitive sharpness.

According to recent reports, tuesday's meeting with PSV represented another chance to demonstrate his readiness for a more prominent role. Instead, his involvement ended after 45 minutes as Mourinho turned to the partnership that has largely carried Madrid's defence this season.

The Brazilian's limited playing time makes the manager's comments about rhythm particularly relevant. Regaining his previous level requires regular appearances, but those opportunities are difficult to obtain while Konate and Huijsen continue to perform.

Huijsen's emergence has already complicated Militao's attempts to recover a starting place, with the Spain international establishing himself as a central figure in Mourinho's defensive aims.

Konate, meanwhile, has made a strong impression following his arrival from Liverpool, offering the combination of athleticism and defensive aggression that the Portuguese coach values.

The two established internationals therefore face different uncertainties. Rudiger must consider his future as his contract approaches its conclusion, while Militao has more time remaining on his deal but needs to demonstrate that he can compete consistently for a starting position.

Mourinho has not unveiled plans to sell either defender, and Tuesday's substitutions should not be regarded as confirmation of their departures.

However, the manager's unusually explicit assessment of his centre-backs has reinforced the challenge facing both players: Konate and Huijsen currently possess the match rhythm, tactical qualities and established partnership that make them difficult to displace.

  • Fabian Hurzeler will let Pascal Gross decide if he needs a rest ahead of Brighton's clash with Craiova to the experienced midfielder himself.
  • The 35-year-old has been an ever-present for the Seagulls this season, starting all 18 of his appearances across the Premier League, Conference League and Carabao Cup.
  • Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Fabian Hurzeler will let Pascal Gross decide if he needs a rest ahead of Brighton's clash with Craiova to the experienced midfielder himself.

The 35-year-old has been an ever-present for the Seagulls this season, starting all 18 of his appearances across the Premier League, Conference League and Carabao Cup.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Gross has accumulated 1,526 minutes of football in all competitions, underlining his importance to Hurzeler's side and the workload he has carried during the campaign.

The German midfielder has been key since returning to the Amex from Borussia Dortmund, but with Brighton facing another managing his fitness is becoming an increasingly notable consideration - especially with Newcastle at the Amex Stadium this Sunday,.

Hurzeler, speaking ahead of the meeting with Romanian league leaders Craiova, remarked: "We are in communication, and I think the only person who can really listen to himself is himself,” said the German.

"I know he's an experienced player, so if the time comes, we will have that conversation and, of course, make the decision.

"He's a clear team player, so if he feels he can't play at his highest level because of his physical condition or because he's tired in certain moments, then he will speak up.

"We have a very trusting relationship, so we will make the decision together.".

Gross has already demonstrated remarkable durability this season and whether Thursday's European fixture provides the moment for a rest remains to be seen.

Injuries will also play a factor in Hurzeler’s thinking. Malick Yalcouye is out for “several weeks” with a knee issue and as yet, midfielder Mats Wieffer has not been added to the Conference League squad.

“I'm not really sure,” said Hurzeler to Sussex World when asked if they can include Wieffer and perhaps Yankuba Minteh to the Uefa list.

“We're trying to get an understanding of how things can work regarding this, but I can't say anything so far because we're still discussing what the best way to solve it is.

“He's definitely out for the next three Conference League games, but hopefully there's another possibility to replace him.”.

Diego Gomez and Olivier Boscagli are also sidelined for this one, while Chema Andres - who played in the 2-0 loss at Hull - is managing his fitness after withdrawing from Spain’s under-21 squad at the previous international break.

Yasin Ayari is also a midfield option for tonight.

As it stands, the Reds have two out-and-out strikers, Danilo Orsi and Pemi Aderoju, while Dylan Morgan, Ade Adeyemo and Stephen Duke-McKenna could all play in that role if needed.

Speaking after the Reds’ battling 0-0 draw with 2nd-placed Barnet on Tuesday night, which extended Blackwell’s unbeaten league record since he arrived, he stated “We tried to go with two strikers, but I’m not sure that game after game after game suits a couple of them.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Sources indicate that "I looked at the bench and there was nothing I could do. I tried to bring Osman (Kamara) to play up top and he naturally drifted out wide left and I didn’t want that.

“I wanted him to play as a two and he’s got to learn a lesson that when he goes on and he’s asked to do a job, do your job – and that’s what frustrates me a little bit.

In a recent development, "We didn’t have an actual sort of midfielder to come in and play. I think Dukey (Duke-McKenna) started to drift a little bit out to the right and I wanted him in alongside Kai, but once again, Dukey came in and did a job for me, pressed as hard as he could.

“So, I can’t complain. It was a situation that if we’d stated before the game that we’d remain unbeaten, you’d have been happy with that. So, we’re unbeaten and I’m happy with that.”.

It has been revealed that since Blackwell took over from Colin Kazim-Richards, Crawley have won two and drawn two, scoring four goals and conceding only two. The Reds are now level on points with Rotherham in 23rd with a game in hand, and only two points behind Rochdale in 22nd with two games in hand.

When asked if he has started looking at bringing anyone in to help out in the Janury transfer eindow, Blackwell noted “To be fair, we were here from 12 o’clock today.

"We brought some new scouts in, a new recruitment guy and we had five hours today before the game kicked off looking at potential targets for January, and the club’s well on its way to do that.”.

While the Nye Camp boss concedes the Rocks will respect Elliot Powell’s side, he will ask his charges to concentrate on their own game initiative in the Isthmian South Central division clash between the second-placed Channel Islanders and Bognor Regis Town, who are third.

Hollands’ men go into the keenly anticipated showdown on the back of a hard-fought 2-1 home win over an in-form Hayes & Yeading United outfit last time out.

Goals from Luke Roberts and Henry McDonald secured the victory and a vital three points that keep the home side in the reckoning at the top end of the standings — and Hollands believes a win is in his side’s grasp at the Springfield Stadium.

The most recent triumph — which came after a home win over Littlehampton Town — further addressed a mini-slump in the league and the gaffer claims his charges should take the positives from getting back on track.

By Matt Law | 25 Nov 2026 21:08, Last updated: 25 Nov 2026 21:10.

Alexander Isak has now registered in his last six away appearances for Liverpool, with the Sweden international on the scoresheet in Wednesday's Champions League clash with Club Brugge.

The 27-year-old made the breakthrough in the 13th minute of the European fixture, with Liverpool leading 1-0 at the interval.

In the Premier League era, the only player to score in six or more successive away outings for Liverpool is Mohamed Salah, who managed seven between August and October 2021.

Isak is now on nine goals in 16 appearances for Andoni Iraola's side this season, including two in four outings in the Champions League.

The striker has also netted seven times in 10 Premier League appearances, with his Liverpool career well and truly underway after a tough 2025-26.

Isak only netted four times in 22 appearances for the Merseyside giants last season, struggling with injury problems, but he has been in impressive form this term.

Liverpool beat Manchester United 4-0 in the Premier League last time out and are on their way to recording a third straight victory in all competitions.

The Reds will follow their European game against Club Brugge with the Merseyside derby, heading to Everton in the Premier League on Sunday afternoon.

Iraola's side will then host Sunderland on December 2, three days before a trip to Chelsea.

Liverpool's next Champions League game is at home to Porto on December 9.

Industry observers note that michael Carrick had urged his Manchester United players to come out and fight. But nobody could have imagined quite how Lisandro Martínez would interpret that message.

By the end of an extraordinary evening in Madrid, where United went 1-0 down inside a minute and never recovered against Atlético Madrid, Martínez had blown the lid off any pretence of all being well at the club as he introduced a lacerating assault on the club’s executives.

United had come into this getting battered from all sides and when Pablo Barrios put Atlético ahead, Jamie Carragher’s pre-match assessment about how things could get “very messy, very rapidly” for all involved at Old Trafford must have been ringing in the ears of the travelling supporters.

Industry observers note that they certainly know how to make life difficult for themselves. Leny Yoro’s 74th-minute red card pretty much ended hopes of them taking something from the game.

Industry observers note that ademola Lookman scored Atlético’s second soon after and Carrick was staring at another defeat. And so they now move on to a big game at Leeds on Sunday. This was not the result Carrick would have wanted – and that is before what happened off the pitch.

Ademola Lookman PUNISHES a 10-man Man United 💥 https://t.co/GHKYIHGhNC.

Another defeat intensified the pressure on Carrick but Martínez left nobody under any illusions that he felt the finger should be pointed not simply at another manager or the players, but the hierarchy above him.

It was extraordinary to see a player speaking out so publicly in this fashion against his own bosses.

But Martínez pulled no punches, even going as far as singling out Jason Wilcox, the director of football, as he criticised the club’s summer transfer business and effectively accused the club of failing Carrick and the players in the window.

To what extent Martínez’s comments mirror the views of the wider dressing room is unclear, but you have to wonder where Carrick and United go from here.

In a recent development, on the one hand, Martínez was providing a show of support for his manager by attacking the people above him. At the same time, he has presented Carrick with a disciplinary problem to address.

Lisandro Martínez did NOT hold back after United's loss to Atletico 😬👀 https://t.co/OGo25Pzd30.

And United have enough troubles as it is without a senior member of Carrick’s dressing room turning so squarely against the club’s power brokers.

Martínez was probably only giving voice to what many fans have been saying since an underwhelming transfer window closed with more questions than answers. But for a player to talk in such blunt, excoriating terms resonated more loudly than anything a supporter or United’s most caustic critic could say.

The message was simple: you can sack all the managers you want but until you pull together a squad worthy of United’s name and give the man at the helm the tools to compete, the club will struggle to escape this cycle of mediocrity.

No one can reasonably argue United’s window was a success. They went into it with the hopes of landing Elliot Anderson and other premium midfielders but ended up going for numbers over proven quality or pedigree. Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Carlos Baleba were not a trio of signings anyone expected at the start of summer, not even the club itself.

There were glaring problems to address in defence, not least at left-back, and at centre-forward but a quality alternative to Luke Shaw never materialised and no back-up was signed for Benjamin Sesko, who was missing for four months with a shin injury that has since resurfaced and which could keep him out for a while yet.

According to recent reports, having done so well to lead United to third and take them back into the Champions League, Carrick would have expected further backing than he got in the summer. Ever the tech giant man, he has been too polite to criticise that lack of investment. But the cat is out of the bag now Martínez has had his say.

It now places the spotlight on Wilcox. United head to Elland Road on Sunday and that was the scene of Rúben Amorim’s final meltdown as manager. Two days after he blew up in a meeting with Wilcox at United’s Carrington training base, Amorim took aim at the director of football and others at the club, demanding they “do their job” and repeatedly declaring that he had come to Old Trafford to “be the manager, not to be the coach”.

It is remarkable to think that, 10 months on, United head back to Leeds with just as many questions as there were back then.

United’s worst start to a league season for 40 years has ensured Carrick is already under pressure, but Martínez is very much of the view that it is no longer enough for the manager and the players to keep carrying the can and that the credibility and suitability of those who recruit the players and make the decisions must now be called into question.

Recent findings suggest that that Martínez picked this game to speak out was interesting. United, lost, yes, and the manner of Atlético’s opening goal from Barrios after 53 seconds was shocking. But United at least went down fighting on this occasion and had fashioned enough good chances to at least draw level before Yoro’s harsh 74th-minute red card swung a delicately poised match decisively in Atlético’s favour.

Lookman made it 2-0 soon after, but Atlético, having looked like they would run all over United in those opening 10 minutes, were made to work hard for their victory.

Sources indicate that united cannot keep shooting themselves in the foot like they did in the first minute. Carrick had gone with a three-man midfield to shore things up and made his team more comfortable and yet they were opened up in double quick time by two passes through the middle.

Still, you only needed to look across at United’s opponents to appreciate how chaotic it had become at Old Trafford.

Diego Simeone’s reign at Atlético covers a period stretching two years longer than the post-Ferguson era and in many ways his teams have represented everything United have not been in that time: well constructed and thought through, unified, stable, organised, hungry, aggressive, uncompromising and with a flash of devilment.

If United were not in crisis before this, they are now.

Man United are in the relegation zone on merit and will need all of Mauricio Pochettino's coaching powers to get them out of it - they are chronically short of form and have forgotten how to win, writes CHRIS WHEELER

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 02:00 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 10:28 EST, 24 November 2026.
  • As the fourth goal flew in and Anfield rejoiced once again, Mauricio Pochettino stood on the touchline with his arms folded and turned to the Manchester United bench with an air of resignation.
  • Industry observers note that what can he do to improve this shambles of a team?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 02:00 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 10:28 EST, 24 November 2026.

As the fourth goal flew in and Anfield rejoiced once again, Mauricio Pochettino stood on the touchline with his arms folded and turned to the Manchester United bench with an air of resignation.

Industry observers note that what can he do to improve this shambles of a team? What could anyone do? United could change their head coach every game, but without the tools to do the job, the result will be largely the same.

Chief executive Omar Berrada said in an interview during the week that United have improved since the summer, but who is he trying to kid? They are in the relegation zone on merit, and it will need all of Pochettino's coaching powers to get them out of it.

He emerged from the tunnel shortly before 4.30pm here dressed smartly in blue, and after greeting Andoni Iraola and his staff, spent a few moments gathering his thoughts while You'll Never Walk Alone echoed around Anfield.

The game plan was in tatters inside 13 minutes, though, as he watched United go two goals and one man down. There was much finger wagging from Pochettino when Leny Yoro was somewhat harshly sent off, but the decision was never going to be overturned and nor should it be used to mask another United debacle.

As the enormity of the task he has taken on dawned upon him in the second half, the Liverpool fans taunted: 'Poch is the wheel.'.

Mauricio Pochettino's first game as Man United head coach ended in a 4-0 defeat at Liverpool.

The manner of the display was a microcosm of why United are mired in the relegation zone.

Pochettino made two changes to the line-up from Michael Carrick's last game in charge against Aston Villa, and the biggest of them backfired spectacularly.

Giving Matthijs de Ligt his Premier League start for more than a year against Liverpool at Anfield felt like a gamble as he replaced Harry Maguire in central defence.

'When I saw Matthijs de Ligt's name on the team-sheet I was absolutely stunned,' admitted former United defender Gary Neville on Sky Sports, citing De Ligt's performance on his only start since last November in the Champions League defeat by Como in October.

However, the Dutchman was at fault for misreading the situation that led to Yoro being sent off in the eighth minute for the foul on Alexander Isak that saw Dominik Szoboszlai fire Liverpool ahead from a free-kick, and was the nearest United defender to Florian Wirtz when he hooked in the second shortly afterwards.

De Ligt got away with falling flat on his face and allowing Isak a free run on goal just after the hour mark, but couldn't stop Bradley Barcola's cross going through his legs when Rio Ngumoha scored the third shortly afterwards.

The nightmare was complete when his ill-judged pass to Joshua Zirkzee let in Liverpool for Victor Munoz to make it 4-0.

Pochettino's other change was to leave out Amad Diallo - who has claimed a couple of memorable goals against Liverpool but hasn't scored for United in nearly a year - and play Patrick Dorgu on the left.

Dorgu returned from injury to head a dramatic late equaliser in Carrick's final game in charge, but he was deemed to be unfit for duty by Denmark who sent him home during the international break.

He started on the left side of attack but switched to left-back when Yoro was sent off and Pochettino reshuffled what is statistically the worst defence in Europe as he tried to avoid a bloodbath.

Matthijs de Ligt (right) endured a nightmare game at centre-back as United were thumped.

Pochettino's response to a horror start was to send on Maguire for Bryan Mbeumo, his best attacker, to provide extra protection for De Ligt.

Industry observers note that having started the game in United's familiar 4-2-3-1 formation, he switched to 5-3-1. Moving to a back-five when your team only has 10 men felt like damage limitation.

It needed some excellent saves from Senne Lammens - not to mention a crucial block by Maguire to send Isak's effort over the bar before half-time - to spare United from an embarrassing defeat on a par with the seven and five goal humiliations at the hands of Liverpool in recent years.

Even so, after seeing his team record a pitiful xG of 0.14 in a first half that saw United have one shot on target and four touches in the Liverpool box, he knew they had to pose more of an attacking threat if only to relieve the pressure on their defence.

Zirkzee replaced the anonymous Matheus Cunha at half-time in the hope that he could hold the ball up better, but the xG rose only marginally to 0.63 by the end compared to Liverpool's 4.38.

Pochettino sent on Mason Mount and Noussair Mazraoui for Youri Tielemans and Dorgu in the 65th minute, and they had only been on the pitch for a matter of seconds when Ngumoha got Liverpool's third.

Senne Lammens produced multiple save to prevent the scoreline from further embarrasment.

There are so many problems piled up for Pochettino, it will be difficult to know where to start when he returns to his desk at Carrington on Monday ahead of this week's Champions League tie against Sporting Lisbon in Portugal.

Industry observers note that this is a team chronically short of form and confidence that has forgotten how to win. There are only so many changes he can make with the squad available until the January transfer window, so the Argentine is stuck with what he's got until then.

But United have simply got to stop giving up early goals. It was a problem that plagued Carrick against Atletico Madrid, Como, Roma and Villa, and any hope that Pochettino could stop the rot disappeared inside eight minutes here.

Yoro's red card was also United's fourth in the last eight games (and his second), which is another bad habit they will have to kick if Pochettino is going to turn this season from hell around.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, accurately predicting protein structures has been the preserve of specialist AI tools like AlphaFold — but now general-purpose models are catching up.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, accurately predicting protein structures has been the preserve of specialist AI tools like AlphaFold — but now general-purpose models are catching up. Credit: EMBL-EBI (CC0).

Recent findings suggest that earlier this month, Xinming Tu set out to test what artificial-intelligence models know about proteins. Tu, a researcher at an AI biology manufacturer called Phylo in South San Francisco, California, asked large language models (LLMs) from OpenAI, Anthropic and Google to predict the sequences of obscure bacterial proteins.

He left the analysis to run overnight and woke up shocked at the results. The latest versions of Anthropic’s Claude models had outperformed other LLMs — but also specialized ‘protein language models’, which are trained on vast troves of sequence data and specially designed for such tasks.

Scientists are using AI to dream up revolutionary upcoming proteins.

Scientists are using AI to dream up revolutionary latest proteins.

When Tu and Leo Chen, a computational biologist at Harvard Medical School in Boston, Massachusetts, shared the results in a 16 November blogpost, it set off a frenzy among computational biologists to see what other protein biology LLMs such as Claude could do. For instance, Tu and Chen and others have found it could perform a key step in protein-structure prediction.

And on 24 November, OpenAI announced that its latest language models had successfully designed newly introduced proteins, some of which behaved as expected when made and tested in the lab. The results hint that the latest LLMs might be gaining a sophisticated understanding of protein biology.

The research has kicked off a debate over the future of biological AI. Some scientists predict that ‘general purpose’ models such as Claude and ChatGPT will eventually outperform specialist tools such as AlphaFold at tasks including protein structure prediction and design.

“We want to see a world where a scientist can just describe in natural language what they want a ChatGPT model to do, and the model can just be infinitely flexible and design exactly what the person wants,” notes Joy Jiao, who leads life-sciences research at OpenAI in San Francisco, California.

Industry observers note that but some researchers question the extent to which LLMs are learning underlying lessons in protein biology. They suggest that some of their abilities could be the result of regurgitating training data.

The release of AlphaFold2, Google DeepMind’s blockbuster protein-structure-prediction AI, in 2020 introduced a revolution in biological AI. There is now a vast ecosystem of software — much of it open source — for modelling different properties of proteins, such as how they interact with possible drugs, and for designing new proteins.

In a recent development, researchers have begun using LLMs to orchestrate these specialist models, but it has mostly been as a time-saving measure, says Martin Pačesa, a structural biologist at the University of Zurich. “In most cases, a specialist will always perform better than a generalist for a given task,” he says.

Five protein-design questions that still challenge AI.

Five protein-design questions that still challenge AI.

Industry observers note that to see if an LLM could stand in for specialist protein-design tools, Jiao and her colleagues asked an OpenAI model called GPT-6.2 to design 3D protein structures capable of binding to five different biological targets, including proteins implicated in cancer and immune disorders. After the LLMs generated the designs, the researchers used a specialist AI tool to determine a corresponding genetic sequence. Lab experiments confirmed that around 11% of designs were able to bind their target.

Sources indicate that in other experiments, the OpenAI team indicated that its LLMs could design protein sequences, redesign existing antibodies, and other tasks typically performed by specialist tools. In some cases, the LLM performed as well as some specialist tools, and in others, such as predicting the 3D structure of proteins, it was far off. OpenAI researchers describe the work in a blogpost and technical paper.

According to recent reports, jiao emphasizes that the work is a proof of principle, and that specialized AI tools were still needed for key steps. But Masatoshi Uehara, an OpenAI researcher who was part of the effort, believes that LLMs will only get better at protein biology. “I believe the large language model can technically beat every specialized model in even each capability,” he claims.

Jude Bellingham backed to become England's greatest ever player amid Premier League 'travesty'

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Real Madrid midfielder Jude Bellingham has been tipped to become England's greatest ever player by former Tottenham Hotspur midfielder Jamie O'Hara, who believes the 23-year-old is already a better footballer than Harry Kane.
  • Bellingham produced another outstanding Champions League performance on Tuesday, scoring a spectacular goal and providing an assist in Real Madrid's 5-1 victory over PSV Eindhoven at the Bernabeu.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Naim Beneddra | 25 Nov 2026 21:20.

Real Madrid midfielder Jude Bellingham has been tipped to become England's greatest ever player by former Tottenham Hotspur midfielder Jamie O'Hara, who believes the 23-year-old is already a better footballer than Harry Kane.

Bellingham produced another outstanding Champions League performance on Tuesday, scoring a spectacular goal and providing an assist in Real Madrid's 5-1 victory over PSV Eindhoven at the Bernabeu.

The England international improvised a remarkable volley with the outside of his boot after the ball bounced back towards him on the edge of the penalty area, later describing the strike as the best goal of his career.

His performance prompted an enthusiastic reaction from O'Hara, whose admiration for Bellingham is accompanied by a growing frustration that English football supporters have never had the opportunity to watch him regularly in the Premier League.

Speaking on talkSPORT's The Sports Bar, O'Hara made a bold prediction about Bellingham's international career.

In a recent development, "He's going to be England's greatest ever player. Ever. He's better than Harry Kane, a better player than Kane," the former Tottenham midfielder noted.

In a recent development, coming from a former Spurs player, the comparison carries weight given Kane's achievements for both club and country. England's all-time leading goalscorer has established himself as one of the finest centre-forwards of his generation, although Bellingham's influence on matches comes from a different position.

The Real Madrid midfielder has registered seven goals and five assists in 18 appearances across all competitions this season, with only Kylian Mbappe directly contributing to more goals for Los Blancos in La Liga.

In a recent development, his ability to influence proceedings from midfield while regularly producing decisive contributions in the final third makes him a valuable player for England. By the time Euro 2028 comes around, Bellingham should be approaching the peak years of his career, with considerable experience of European football already behind him.

O'Hara also described it as a "travesty" that Premier League supporters do not get to watch the midfielder in domestic action every week. However, fellow pundit Jason Cundy suggested that Bellingham's decision to develop his career outside England may have contributed to his success.

Unlike many of England's leading internationals, Bellingham has built his reputation almost entirely outside his homeland. He left Birmingham City for Borussia Dortmund in 2020 at the age of 17 before joining Real Madrid three years later.

His time in Germany allowed him to establish himself as a regular at Champions League level while still a teenager. At Madrid, he won both La Liga and the Champions League in his debut campaign, scoring 23 goals across all competitions.

The prospect of Bellingham eventually playing in the Premier League appears increasingly distant, with Real Madrid reportedly in advanced negotiations over a newly introduced long-term contract.

According to The Athletic, the Spanish giants intend to announce an agreement before the end of the calendar year, with Bellingham expected to receive a significant increase on his current annual salary of approximately £12.6m.

His existing deal already runs until June 2029, meaning Real Madrid are under little immediate pressure to negotiate. Their willingness to offer improved terms more than two and a half years before its expiry reflects the importance they attach to retaining the midfielder.

For England, there is little sporting reason to regret Bellingham's absence from the Premier League. He is developing at one of Europe's most demanding clubs and gaining experience in the latter stages of major competitions. The disappointment expressed by O'Hara is understandable from a spectator's perspective, but the Three Lions may benefit from the unconventional route their midfielder has taken.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Celtic have taken a leaf from the Hearts model by taking the plunge into the world of data analytics.

The Scottish champions have declared a strategic partnership with Pluto Data Analytics in a bid to enhance their player recruitment.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

The link-up with the London-based football analytics and predictive modelling company will initially run for three years, with scope for it to be extended.

Celtic’s recruitment strategy has been heavily criticised among supporters in recent seasons amid their struggles in Europe and increased domestic competition from Rangers and Hearts.

The club noted that working with Pluto would allow them to “gain access to enhanced analytical tools and insights to support existing recruitment and football operations functions”.

The move comes two years after Premiership rivals Hearts partnered with Tony Bloom-linked Jamestown Analytics in a deal which helped elevate the Edinburgh club to a level where they were within minutes of winning the title last term.

Announcing their upcoming partnership on Wednesday, Celtic said: “The objective is clear: to improve decision-making, identify emerging opportunities and support the club’s long-term football strategy.”.

Sources indicate that hoops chief executive Michael Nicholson stated: “We are always looking for ways to strengthen our football operation and ensure that we continue to evolve in an increasingly competitive environment. We have been reviewing the options in this area in order to select the optimum model for our club.

“Our partnership with Pluto Data Analytics, an organisation with real quality and pedigree within this field, reflects our commitment to innovation and continuous improvement.

“Recruitment remains one of the most crucial areas of any football club. Our aim is to identify talent as effectively as possible, reduce uncertainty where we can and support our football staff with the best available information.

“We believe this partnership will strengthen our ability to support the Club’s ambitions both domestically and in European competition.”.

Manager Martin O’Neill mentioned: “While football is not an exact science, if the club can access and utilise new tools and new details, ultimately, we hope that such data will help us deliver the success we are all striving for.

“Our recruitment and wider football operations teams have already engaged with Pluto. Our intends in the short, medium and longer term are being developed and we are confident that our relationship will deliver real tangible benefit to the club over the next few years.”.

Jon Godfrey, CEO of Pluto Data Analytics, stated: “We believe that predictive data modelling combined with the allure and resources of such a famous institution will allow us to achieve great things in this partnership.

“Celtic has the capacity to compete at the highest levels of European football and it is an honour and a fantastic challenge to work relentlessly with the club on achieving the exciting goals we have put in place.”.

Formed in 2020, the organization has between 51 and 200 employees, according to its LinkedIn profile, with its office based at Tintagel House, Albert Embankment, London.

While Jamestown Analytics were well known in football circles when they arrived on the scene at Hearts due to their previous work with Brighton and Union Saint-Gilloise, much less is known about Pluto Data Analytics.

Under the 'What We Do' section on their manufacturer website, it states: "At Pluto, we combine sports intuition with the latest technology and massive data sets to answer difficult questions across multiple sports. Our work goes beyond validating player performance: we help clubs find overlooked talent, assess tactical impact and make smarter decisions at every level of the game. From top-tier recruitment to identifying emerging stars in under-scouted leagues, we turn complexity into clarity through intelligent, fast and adaptable data tools.".

Industry observers note that another section of their website, under Bespoke Recruitment, adds: "At Pluto, we use advanced machine learning to validate how a player might adapt in a fresh league. For example, how would a defender in Japan’s J1 League perform in the MLS in America? This kind of insight supports clubs to make smarter, more confident recruitment decisions across borders.".

Celtic are currently the only football club publicly identified as a client of Pluto Data Analytics, although the organization states on its website that its predictive models are used by "clubs around the globe".

Like Jamestown, Pluto also has a background in the betting market, with their website stating: "Our models have been battle-tested by clients in betting markets, validating our edge across multiple sports.".

Industry observers note that in another similarity, Pluto’s CEO, Jon Godfrey, is a former professional poker. Tony Bloom, who founded Jamestown Analytics, also played poker professionally although there is no record of the pair having crossed paths.

After Ashley Nathaniel-George cancelled out Roy Syla’s opener just before half-time, a five minute spree including two goals from John Marquis and an own-goal from Harvey Griffiths turned the tide heavily in favour of the hosts after the interval.

Dominic Johnson-Fisher’s superb showing from the bench brought the Rebels within touching distance of leaving Surrey with a point after the number nine netted twice, but the deficit could not be overturned before the full-time whistle.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

It was the hosts who enjoyed the better start of the two side through 20 minutes, as experienced forward Marquis had two sights on goal early on. A driving run down the right flank by Jaiden Putman inside the first minute led to the former Portsmouth striker being picked out at the far post, yet he could not get an effort away under pressure from multiple Worthing bodies.

Five minutes later, another breakaway for the Cardinals saw Marquis latch onto a lofted ball in behind the Rebels backline. Shaping onto his left side, the 34 year-old’s strike was kept out by the midriff of Harrison Foulkes.

In a recent development, worthing had spells of promise during the early exchanges, with the weekend’s match-winner Jordan Young instrumental once again in most of the away side’s attacking play. The former Torquay United man had his best effort of the half just after quarter of an hour, linking up with Kendall through the right channel before firing over Vicente Reyes’ crossbar.

According to recent reports, putman’s adventurous play down the Woking right posed a persistent threat to the left of the visitors’ defence throughout the first half. The QPR-loanee tested Foulkes with an attempt of his own with 20 minutes on the clock drifting inward from the right side before being kept out by another Foulkes intervention.

With half an hour on the clock, a double substitution from Hinshelwood to bring on both Cory Adjetey-Brew and Nathaniel-George proved the spark for a crescendo of action to close out the half.

Industry observers note that A loose ball following an aerial challenge allowed Putman to drive forward down the right. The ball found the feet of Josh Kelly at the by-line, who swivelled before picking out the run of Syla into the box. With Syla unmarked, the midfielder side-footed the ball past Foulkes to open the scoring.

According to recent reports, woking’s first half advantage did not last long, and it was one of the two first half changes in Nathaniel-George who fashioned an equaliser with a minute of normal time remaining in the period. Cutting in from the left flank, the substitute curled a right-footed strike which nestled into Reyes’ bottom left corner from 20 yards out. A spectacular way to open his goalscoring account for the Rebels.

While Worthing’s rapid response may have spurned optimism amongst the travelling faithful heading into the break, the start of the second half spelled nothing but turmoil from a Worthing perspective.

Less than a minute after play resumed, Marquis notched his second of the night after turning the ball home from the edge of the six-yard box with a flicked finish amidst a sea of away defenders.

Industry observers note that the hosts doubled their advantage almost immediately after regaining their lead. A poorly-executed pass from Foulkes invited Woking to spring an attack, and with the visitors’ keeper stranded off his goal-line, Marquis swept home into an empty net to make it 3-1.

Recent findings suggest that five minutes of horror to start the half culminated with the home side adding a fourth goal. Another giveaway in midfield presented Josh Grant the opportunity to drive towards the box. Grant’s eventual effort fizzed off the foot of the retreating Griffiths, with Foulkes helpless to watch the ball trickle over the line.

Recent findings suggest that the away contingent stunned following a flurry of concessions, Hinshelwood looked to the bench yet again for inspiration in giving the Rebels a chance of coming away with something. One of those introductions was Johnson-Fisher, who netted two brilliant goals to bring the visitors back to within one.

In a recent development, in the 64th minute, a ball in from the left side was brought down astutely by the former Whitehawk striker, who fired the ball home on the turn off the underside of the crossbar. Then, 12 minutes later, another fine finish from Johnson-Fisher gave Worthing their third, this time getting on the end of a low pass in behind from Nathaniel-George before slotting a low drive underneath the body of Reyes.

Ultimately, despite the visitors’ best efforts in the closing stages. three goals in rapid succession to start the second half proved too much for the away side to overcome on a cold Tuesday night of madness at the Kingfield Stadium.

It will be the only time the Hoops have faced an opponent from the second tier of their domestic league in a Uefa competition as a result of Torreense claiming the first major trophy in the club's 109-year history last season.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Industry observers note that their shock 2-1 victory over Sporting Lisbon in the final of the Portuguese Cup in May to qualify for Europe for the first time in their history was the stuff of fairtytale. Think second tier Raith Rovers beating Celtic in the League Cup final in 1994.

Recent findings suggest that of course, by the time Raith came to play in the UEFA Cup the following season, they had gone on to earn promotion to the top flight. Not so Torreense. They lost 2-0 on aggregate to Casa Pia in the promotion/relegation play-off, meaning they remained in Liga Portugal 2 for the 2026/27 campaign.

They have since parted tech giant with their cup-winning manager Luís Tralhão, who was sacked last month after overseeing a poor start to the domestic season, and replaced him with former Estrela da Amadora boss João Nuno.

Torreense presently occupy a lowly 13th spot in Liga Portugal 2 and will host Celtic in Leiria, 60 miles away from their home in Torres Vedras, as their own stadium only has 2,500 seats and does not meet Uefa requirements.

But park any thoughts of this fixture providing a banker win for Celtic. Torreense have already beaten Lillestrom and Ararat-Armenia in the Europa League and took the lead against Sunderland before the Premier League side netted a stoppage-time winner.

They sit 19th in the Europa League table, a lofty 13 places above Celtic, who belatedly put their first points on the board with a 3-2 win over Besiktas on November 5 after losing to Ferencváros, Benfica and Celta Vigo.

Nonetheless, this is a match Celtic should be looking to win if they are to retain realistic ambitions of becoming the first team to reach the knockout phase of the competition after losing their opening three league phase matches.

This is their most winnable tie on paper and failure to garner three points would leave Martin O'Neill's men with minimal margin for error in their remaining three fixtures - away to Omonoia, home to Marseille, then away to Union Saint-Gilloise.

It has been revealed that ten points, and a reasonably healthy goal difference is expected to be the benchmark for reaching the knockout play-off round. Nine points may be enough, but 11 points is the target to be absolutely sure.

Celtic should be looking at trips to Torreense and Omonoia, at the moment fifth in the Cypriot league, as an opportunity to reach nine points before facing the French and Belgian major-hitters in their final two matches.

Industry observers note that A familiar face awaits them at the Dr. Magalhães Pessoa Stadium. Former Hearts striker Musa Drammeh has been with the Portuguese club since departing Tynecastle in the summer of 2025.

He was part of their cup-winning squad last season and has played 17 times this term, scoring two goals.

The 24-year-old Spaniard has history with Celtic, having made his SPFL debut against them in a 2-0 defeat at Parkhead in September 2024, and then scoring his first Hearts goal in a 4-1 loss at Tynecastle two months later.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This one was not a match for the football connoisseur – but was one for fans of never-say-die defending as Broadbridge Heath put on a tenacious display of defending against promotion hopefuls Erith Town on a bitter cold Tuesday evening at the JM Clark Stadium.

Chris Simmons’ Heath side knew it would be a difficult match up against a Dockers side on top form, second in the division with games in-hand and with the best home record in the division having played eight and won all eight.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

But it was the Bears who had the first shot on target on 9 minutes when Sam Hards was brought down some 30 yards from goal and Ben Royall stepped up to take the resulting free-kick – hitting a left foot shot that was saved comfortably low to his left by the Dockers goalkeeper Javern Pitterson.

On 16 minutes Erith were awarded a free-kick wide on the right and just outside the penalty area, James Dyer played the ball into the danger area where it pinged in and around the 6 yard box before being cleared by Brad Peters and that set the tone for the first half with the hosts having most of the play but unable to break down the solid Bears defence.

Broadbridge Heath did have a few chances, Royall tried to catch Pitterson out with a shot to the near-post but the keeper got back to gather and Ollie Rawlins had a left foot shot saved by Pitterson diving low to his left and it was 0-0 at the break.

The Dockers stepped up a gear in the second half, kicking down the slope, and had the Bears pinned back in their own half for long periods but without really troubling goalkeeper Alfie Hadfield, plenty of goal attempts but everyone charged down by a Broadbridge Heath player defending like their lives depended on it.

On 75 minutes a rare foray deep into the Erith half saw Charlie Connell brought down by a clumsy challenge some 25 yards from goal, Ben Royal stepped up to take the resulting free-kick striking a left foot shot that deflected off the wall wrong-footing Pitterson who could do nothing but watch the ball fly into the net out of his reach.

The hosts continued to push players forward in search of an equaliser but just couldn’t get past the Broadbridge Heath defensive lines who stood firm and dealt with everything the Dockers could throw at them – and it remained 0-1 at the final whistle with Heath continuing their remarkable run of having scored in every league game this season.

Simmons said afterwards: “This one was a bit of a smash and grab, Erith are a very good side and should of gone in front in the first half, defensively we were excellent and our shape and organisation was top notch and in the end got the lucky break the lads deserved.”.

Next up for the Bears is the visit of division leaders Faversham Town to the Air Engineering Stadium on Saturday.

BBH: Hadfield, Cotton, Royall, Marino, Peters, Richardson, Connell, Bejashvili (Doughty 71), Rawlins, Holden, Hards.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Alphadjo Cisse is one goal away from double figures for the season, and we have not even reached the end of November yet.

In a recent development, as La Gazzetta dello Sport write, the numbers that Cisse is putting up are those of a centre-forward. He has six goals in 10 Serie A appearances, at an average of one every 74 minutes. In the Europa League he has three (a hat-trick against RB Salzburg), at one every 84 minutes.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Yet, his role remains a bit of a mystery. Cisse has his own idea of ​​his preferred position on the pitch, even if he’s a bit vague. Speaking after the match against Frosinone, he hinted that he’d like to move into the attacking midfielder position behind the striker.

Sources indicate that “I’d have more fun and entertain the fans. It would also be easier to provide assists for my team-mates, something I enjoy and haven’t yet managed to do at AC Milan,” he confessed to Sky.

In Verona’s youth team, where Cisse first emerged, head coach Paolo Sammarco deployed him as a left-sided attacking midfielder. It was a position in which the then 17-year-old then went on to score 16 league goals in a breakout season.

Industry observers note that at Catanzaro, in his first professional stint in Serie B under Alberto Aquilani, the Italian played more or less the same role in a 3-4-2-1 system, sometimes a bit wider. Before the serious injury that caused him to miss the final six months of last season, he has scored six goals in 22 games.

According to recent reports, ruben Amorim initially deployed him as a left-sided winger, also due to Christian Pulisic’s temporary unavailability. He would later move him further forward and more centrally, to take up the spaces a striker would, a position he has played for Italy U21s under Silvio Baldini.

According to recent reports, in this position, Cisse can utilise his extraordinary ability to position himself between the ball and the defender, before turning, aiming and often finishing first time. Despite not being physically big (at 180cm tall), he is strong and has a low centre of gravity that makes him tough to bump off the ball.

⚽️ GOAL ALPHADJO CISSE! 🔥 https://t.co/aMIgE9PXHc.

— SempreMilan (@SempreMilanCom) November 22, 2026.

This is where the dilemma arises. At Verona and Catanzaro, Alphadjo Cisse impressed because of his speed and agility. After the injury and under the watch of Amorim, he has become more of a positioning-based player, barely ever tearing down the flank.

In a recent development, so far this season, he’s attempted only 16 dribbles at just over three per game, and has only succeeded on five. With one successful dribble per game on average, his success rate is just over 31% (FotMob data).

These numbers perhaps help explain Cisse’s progression close to the penalty area, and also a concept that the player himself has repeated in recent months regarding where he is at in his personal development. On Sunday, he declared: “I’m not even halfway to my potential.”.

Who knows if Alpha is referring to his overall growth, with horizons still unexplored, or perhaps his post-injury recovery. Amorim will continue to ponder things, but this is far from a headache, because the rule seems to be well established: if Cisse plays, he tends to score.

A 1-1 draw against Norwegian side Nordsjælland at Tynecastle was followed by away defeats at Trabzonspor (2-0) and FC Thun (3-1) to leave the Tynecastle club facing an uphill task to qualify for the knockout stages.

Teams typically need seven or eight points from their six league phase matches to finish inside the top 24 and reach the knockout play-off round. Eight points virtually guarantees progression, while seven points usually puts a club right on the cut-off line where tie-breakers decide who advances.

Hearts know this only too well, having failed to progress on goals scored after collecting seven points to finish 25th during their 2024-25 Conference League campaign.

According to recent reports, monaco arrive in Edinburgh fourth in the table with a maximum haul of nine points following victories over CSKA Sofia, Nordsjælland and Freiburg. Their domestic form has been less impressive of late with Filipe Luís’ side right now on a five-game winless run on Ligue 1, where they are eighth in the standings.

The Conference League match between Hearts and Monaco takes place at Tynecastle Park, Edinburgh, on Thursday, November 26, 2026. Kick-off is 5.45pm.

The match will be shown live on TNT Sports 3 with coverage starting at 5pm.

Fans can stream the match live via HBO Max or Amazon Prime Video with a TNT Sports subscription.

Free highlights will be posted on the TNT Sports Football YouTube channel shortly after full-time.

Recent findings suggest that hearts welcome midfielder Blair Spittal back into their Europa League squad following his recovery from an ankle injury. Malachi Fagan-Walcott drops out with a groin problem. Two players who featured in the 8-0 win over Dundee on Saturday, Eduardo Ageu and Leart Kabashi, cannot play as they are not registered in the Europa League squad list.

Sources indicate that midfielder Tomas Magnusson is still completing concussion protocol before he can be declared available. Defender Craig Halkett and the versatile Oisin McEntee were back on the Riccarton training pitch on Wednesday, although they will not be back until next month. Winger Calvin Miller has also undergone surgery on his knee and will be out for between six weeks and two months.

Stephen Kingsley (hamstring), Harry Milne (knee) and Tom Renaud (ankle) are also unavailable.

It has been revealed that monaco are without five players. Goalkeeper Philippe Kohn, defender Mohammed Salisu, midfielders Stanis Idumbo and Aleksandr Golovin, plus forward Paris Brunner were all left in the Principality for treatment.

Recent findings suggest that an all-German officiating team will take charge of the match. Daniel Schlager is the on-field referee and will be supported on the touchlines by assistant referees Sven Waschitzki and Tobias Fritsch. Robin Braun has been appointed as the fourth official. In the video operations room, Benjamin Cortus will serve as the Video Assistant Referee (VAR), alongside Nicolas Winter as the Assistant VAR (AVAR).

Industry observers note that di Paola told us: “I don’t think we played particularly well. I can’t argue with the scoreline. There are no real arguments, really. I think they were the better team.

It has been revealed that “The pitch meant you couldn’t really play any football, but that suited them. I’m not a football snob. There’s no wrong or right way of playing football. The way they play is effective and works for them.

Recent findings suggest that “We tried to play the same way as them but we weren’t brave enough and it played into their hands. They were always going to be better at that kind of football than us.
