Celtic are in Europa League action on Thursday night when they travel to Portugal to face second-tier side Torreense.

The game will mark the first time in history that the Hoops have contested a European fixture against a team who are not competing in the top flight of their domestic league.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Torreense qualified for the Europa League after a fairytale cup success last season, defying the odds to beat Sporting Lisbon in the final of the Portuguese Cup to claim the first major trophy in their 109-year existence.

They failed to secure promotion, however, losing 2-0 on aggregate to Casa Pia in the promotion/relegation play-off, meaning they remained in Liga Portugal 2 for the 2026/27 campaign, where they current sit 13th in the table.

Celtic put their first Europa League points on the board at the fourth attempt with a 3-2 win over Besiktas on November 5 following three consecutive defeats by Ferencvaros, Benfica and Celta Vigo.

Martin O’Neill’s side sit 32nd in the 36-team league with four games to play as they bid to climb into the top 24 and become the first side to qualify for the knockout stages after losing their opening three league phase matches.

Torreense are in a healthier 19th position having collected six points from their opening four games with victories over Lillestrom and Ararat-Armenia mixed with defeats to Sunderland and Ferencvaros.

The Europa League match between Torreense and Celtic will take place on Thursday, November 26, 2026 at the Dr. Magalhães Pessoa Stadium in Leiria. The venue is 60 miles away from Torreense’s actual home in Torres Vedras, as their own stadium only has 2,500 seats and does not meet Uefa requirements. Kick-off is 8pm.

The match will be shown live on TNT Sports 3 with coverage starting at 7.45pm, following on from Hearts v Monaco on the same channel.

Fans can stream the match live via HBO Max or Amazon Prime Video with a TNT Sports subscription.

Free highlights will be posted on the TNT Sports Football YouTube channel shortly after full-time.

It has been revealed that celtic have added Jota to their Europa League squad in place of the injured Mika Baur. The Portuguese winger was initially left out as he fought his way back from a serious knee injury. But he could now feature in his homeland against Torreense after continuing his comeback with a start in Saturday’s 4-1 win over St Mirren. Baur was recently ruled out for up to 10 weeks with ankle ligament damage.

Benjamin Nygren is nursing a heel problem while Alistair Johnston remains sidelined by a hamstring injury.

Torreense are missing suspended Jorge Aguirre following his red card in the 3-2 win over Aararat-Armenia and the injured Adama Baradji.

Industry observers note that an all-Dutch officiating team will take charge of the match. Allard Lindhout is the on-field referee and he will be joined on the pitch by assistant referees Johan Balder and Murat Kucukerbir, while Jannick van der Laan serves as the fourth official. Pol van Boekel has been assigned as the Video Assistant Referee (VAR) with Dennis Johan Higler acting as the Assistant Video Assistant Referee (AVAR).

Torreense 4/1, Draw 7/2, Celtic 4/6 - via oddschecker.com.

#130412. I was in the room with Newcastle bosses as they were grilled by fans on Matthias Jaissle, their January transfer plans and the new stadium - here's what they had to say, and my verdict: CRAIG HOPE

📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1454 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dailymail ↗ Open Full Page

I was in the room with Newcastle bosses as they were grilled by fans on Matthias Jaissle, their January transfer plans and the new stadium - here's what they had to say, and my verdict: CRAIG HOPE

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1454 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 07:00 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 10:59 EST, 24 November 2026.
  • Newcastle United’s hierarchy addressed supporters at a ‘United We Stand’ event in the shadow of St James’ Park this week.
  • Chief executive David Hopkinson, sporting director Ross Wilson, chief financial officer Simon Capper and chief operating officer Brad Miller were on stage discussing head coach Matthias Jaissle, transfers and the prospect of a fresh stadium.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By CRAIG HOPE, CHIEF FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 07:00 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 10:59 EST, 24 November 2026.

Newcastle United’s hierarchy addressed supporters at a ‘United We Stand’ event in the shadow of St James’ Park this week.

Chief executive David Hopkinson, sporting director Ross Wilson, chief financial officer Simon Capper and chief operating officer Brad Miller were on stage discussing head coach Matthias Jaissle, transfers and the prospect of a fresh stadium.

Our chief football reporter, Craig Hope, was also in the room, and here is his rundown of all the key topics….

‘Arsenal (2-2 draw) felt like a real step forward in the second-half, you felt the energy change in the stadium. But as positive as it was, the biggest feeling we have right now is one of frustration, because the first half wasn't good.

Industry observers note that ‘We have seen that a few times already this season. An outstanding first half against Hull and a difficult second half. Maybe at Tottenham, 90 minutes straight, really good. Crystal Palace, the second-half very good, first half not.

‘So we're definitely trying to find consistency and Saturday was positive. The team felt like they owed that performance to the fans in the second-half. The frustration is that we didn't see that for 90 minutes.’.

Sporting director Ross Wilson and chief executive David Hopkinson were among the members of the Newcastle hierarchy to answer questions from fans on Monday.

The discussion came in the wake of a promising Saturday performance against Arsenal.

HOPE: It would have been easy for Wilson to say, ‘Wasn’t Saturday great? We build from here’. Instead, he gave an honest assessment of where the team is at - because progress cannot really be achieved by playing well for 45 minutes here and there. It felt like a little warning shot, and a fair one.

‘I want to be really clear (about Vision 2030). I think sometimes it has been misreported as, “Oh, I’m guaranteeing we're going to win by 2030”. No, what I have is guaranteed is that we're in the conversation.

Industry observers note that ‘(Re 2.0) We set up with a initiative that was very coherent of what we wanted to accomplish this summer. Not incremental change, but necessary and significant change. We lost three players who were important contributors to the past season.

Recent findings suggest that ‘We set out on a direction under Ross' leadership where we would have a different set of expectations that recognised financial reality. We articulated a vision for the squad here that would be organised around some young talent, who we expect to grow here.

‘So I’m delighted with the job Ross did. We executed that strategy superbly. Not everything that we set out to do was accomplished. We went hard on Johan Manzambi and didn't succeed. We went hard on Victor Munoz, didn't succeed, despite thinking we were going to land both of those at one point. But also had successes that we had not anticipated.’.

Recent findings suggest that HOPE: Wilson also spoke about the strategy of bringing down the squad’s average age, and there appeared to be no panic or concern over the so-far indifferent impact of summer additions. It has been noted by many that on Saturday, in the second half, no upcoming signings were involved apart from goalkeeper Lukas Hornicek. For me, you cannot judge players over three months (look at Lewis Hall) but the big price tags attached to some of the young arrivals has raised expectation. Jaissle and the hierarchy need the likes of Matias Fernandez-Pardo, in particular, to start impacting, if questions over summer business are to quieten.

’In simple terms, the club had maxed out its credit card in the first few years under the latest ownership. We had complied with PSR but it had been incredibly tight, and that forced us to sell at an undervalued price people like Elliot Anderson. We didn’t want to and we didn't want to be there again.

Recent findings suggest that ‘So we had to do something differently. The good news is that the Premier League has changed their rules so that there's a bit more headroom now. We’re comfortably within those and we're also comfortably within what we've agreed with UEFA (Newcastle were fined earlier this year). So we're in a really good place. That's the work that David and Ross had talked about in terms of 2.0.

‘That allows us to actually continue to invest and trade. It means that we've got no imperative to sell somebody in January. And it gives us the ability, depending on where we are in the league at the end of this season, to invest again at a proportionate level, depending on what European competition you qualify for.’.

HOPE: The message was clear - there is scope to spend in January and next summer. Newcastle should use that to target goals in the Fresh Year.

Upcoming Magpies coach Mathias Jaissle was also under the microscope in the shadow of St James' Park.

‘Eddie Howe was a workaholic and he put his heart and soul into the job. So we needed someone who would work hard and the players would not notice a drop off. Matthias works incredibly hard.

‘Eddie was also outstanding on the grass, an elite coach. Again, our players couldn't feel, “Eddie’s gone and they've got another guy who doesn't coach”. Matthias is an expert, elite coach.

Recent findings suggest that ‘From a transfer perspective, the head coach at Newcastle always has the final say in any player who comes in. Matthias puts a lot of effort into that - convincing players and making sure they're the right character fit for him. He’s thrown himself into all things Newcastle and we enjoy working with him a lot.’.

‘Matthias is a clear winner. And you know winners, they win over time. I have a high, high conviction we're going to win under his leadership. I don't think I've ever had the conviction more that we're going to win together than I do right now.’.

Industry observers note that HOPE: It is a bold statement from Hopkinson on the back of one win in seven, but the support for Jaissle is clear. He will (and should) be given time, despite an inconsistent start that has included a couple of horror indicates. It was also interesting to note Wilson’s reference to Jaissle’s heavy involvement in transfers, on the back of a week in which the head coach let it be known he wanted more control over transfers.

‘This decision is going to last forever. It will outlast our lifetime. It’s that enormity that means we are taking a little bit of time now.

‘Is it going to allow us to compete with the top clubs? Are we going to be able to do it from a financial perspective? Is it going to be transformative for all of our fans, the city and for the region? For all of those reasons, we are very purposely taking our time. But whether we stay at St James’ Park or move, it will be absolutely fantastic.’.

Newcastle continue to mull key decisions on the renovation of their stadium in a bid to unlock fresh revenue for the club.

‘We need it (larger stadium) for the revenue a new stadium will unlock. This is a generational decision and will define the next era of this club. It’s going to be really expensive. We’re advancing significantly into clearly defined options. This is a project with global significance.

In a recent development, ‘We've spent a lot of time with New York bankers recently thinking through how we might do this and what options we can consider. I can assure you we're working on this every day. I hope we will have something concrete to share with you soon.’.

HOPE: There was ‘no update’ but the subtext of the discussion was very definitely geared towards a new stadium. I understand this is the direction of travel now, and Hopkinson confirming our story from last week about the high-level talks with Goldman Sachs over how to finance a new stadium demonstrates how advanced the project is.

Overall, the tone of the night was one of ‘we have a plan, stick with us’. It was very different 12 months ago, when the mood in the room was one of huge optimism and excitement at the unveiling of a new executive team ahead of a Champions League campaign.

In a recent development, now, it feels like all involved - supporters and those on the inside - realise that this part of the journey will not be easy. That was reflected in the message conveyed.

The former England striker, turned broadcaster, was discussing Fabian Hürzeler's side on The Rest is Football podcast – following Albion’s disappointing 2-0 defeat at Hull City. A victory would have taken the high-flying Seagulls to within three points to leaders Arsenal.

Brighton produced some impressive football but were unable to find a way past an inspired opposition goalkeeper, in Konstantinos Tzolakis. Their failure to convert chances proved costly, with Oli McBurnie stealing the game with a late brace.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

In a recent development, despite the result, Lineker was left hugely impressed by what he saw from the Seagulls. He described Brighton as the ‘best team to watch in the league’ when it comes to the quality of football.

The former Tottenham and Barcelona striker said he believes the addition of a clinical centre-forward could make Albion a formidable proposition.

"If Brighton had a nine like Leicester had in Jamie Vardy, I think they would be serious title challengers," Lineker, 65, noted.

It has been revealed that "They create so many chances. They haven't got, or at least I've not seen, a real nine in there that sniffs out [goals].".

The former Match of the Day host acknowledged that the Seagulls had played some excellent football but could not find the finishing touch.

"I watched the Brighton game yesterday, and I still can't quite work out [how they didn’t score]," he stated.

"Well, I can, because they missed too many chances, and the opposition's keeper was unbelievable, but they played some incredibly good football.

"They couldn't score, which is unusual because they've scored more goals than any other team in the league this season.

"Even though they lost 2-0, I was thinking, God, Brighton are good.

"I go back to the point but if they had someone like a Vardy, wow, they'd be very difficult to stop, I think.".

Regardless, Lineker said he ‘definitely can see’ Brighton in the Champions League next season.

Industry observers note that his fellow podcast pundit Micah Richards agreed with the assessment. But he also felt the result was particularly damaging to Brighton's ambitions.

The former Manchester City full-back suggested that, if the Seagulls were serious about making a push towards the top of the Premier League, winning at Hull was essential.

"I know it's ridiculous – and we're talking about jumping on the bandwagon and being reactionary – but I think for a real push, they had to win that game," he said.

However, Richards, 38, was equally complimentary about the football Hürzeler's team are producing.

"I think they play some of the best football in the Premier League – they create so many chances," he noted.

It has been revealed that he agreed that they ideally need to sign a prolific number nine. But he was keen to stress that the comments were not intended as criticism of Albion’s current forwards – including Georginio Rutter, who started the match at Hull, and Charalampos Kostoulas.

"It's no disrespect to Rutter, he's just not got the clinical edge of a world-class player," Richards explained.

Richards also highlighted the contribution of midfielder Yasin Ayari, particularly his ability to make late runs into the penalty area.

Alan Shearer was another to praise Brighton's performance, describing the quality of their football and the pace at which they moved the ball.

"Great football, some brilliant football. They were passing and moving at pace – superb," the all-time leading Premier League goalscorer mentioned.

Sources indicate that the Newcastle legend added: "It was just one of those days where the keeper had his day and nothing was going to go past him. You have that and you just move on.”.

Shearer, 56, also felt the result should not overshadow the quality of Brighton's display.

"I think he [Hürzeler] will be disappointed with the result, but performance-wise, I thought they were brilliant,” he said.

Brighton were not the only team to receive praise, with Richards also highlighting Bournemouth's recent formidable form.

The podcast trio agreed that the quality across the Premier League is improving, with Richards arguing that teams outside the traditional 'massive six' are becoming increasingly difficult opponents.

Industry observers note that for Brighton, however, Lineker's message was clear. He believes Hürzeler has a side capable of playing some of the best football in the country, but adding a striker with the instincts and finishing ability of Vardy could make them a much more dangerous proposition.

Iraola had said he was not concerned about Barcola’s numbers when Liverpool arrived in Linz, even if no goals and no assists since his £123m move from Paris St-Germain had caused debate, but those numbers look infinitely better now after his first senior hat-trick.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Three astronauts will launch aboard China’s Shenzhou-24 spacecraft.Credit: Xinhua/Shutterstock.

For the first time, China will send a foreign astronaut to its Tiangong space station.

Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, a Pakistani military pilot, is expected to travel to Tiangong on 25 November aboard China’s Shenzhou-24 spacecraft, alongside two Chinese astronauts, known as ‘taikonauts’.

Recent findings suggest that “My first [flight] not only represents myself, but also my country,” Ali told reporters in Mandarin on 24 November at the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Centre in northwest China. Ali has been training intensively in Beijing for the past seven months, including learning Mandarin. He said that he carried “the dream of 250 million Pakistani people” when he entered the training centre.

Sending an astronaut to space is “a huge step” for Pakistan’s space aspirations, claims Wajiha Iqbal, a lunar scientist at the University of Münster in Germany. The partnership enables Pakistan to “do great science in space”, she adds.

In a recent development, the mission is also a milestone for China’s space programme. The country’s expanding capabilities now allow it to offer international partners opportunities that few countries can provide on their own, indicates Yuxuan Jia, who researches China’s foreign policy at the Center for China and Globalization, a think tank in Beijing. The launch signals China’s “aspirations to become a top space power”, Jia says.

Shenzhou-24 is expected to be carried into a low-Earth orbit by China’s Long March-2F rocket, which is scheduled to launch from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Centre at 08:18am local time on 25 November, said Zhang Jingbo, a spokesperson of the China Manned Space Programme, at a press conference on 24 November. Shenzhou-24 is expected to automatically dock with Tiangong (which translates as ‘heavenly palace’) around 3.5 hours after reaching orbit.

Ali will stay on Tiangong for about a week before returning to Earth with two of the three taikonauts currently on the station.

China’s successful launch of Mars mission seals global era in deep-space exploration.

China’s successful launch of Mars mission seals global era in deep-space exploration.

Industry observers note that ali will board Shenzhou-24 as a payload specialist responsible mainly for scientific experiments rather than operating the spacecraft. The mission aims to host four biotechnology experiments developed by universities in Pakistan, Amer Gilani, an official at Pakistan’s space agency told newswire Reuters in September. Details about the research have not yet been made public.

Recent findings suggest that according to Zhang, one goal of this mission is to establish a study of how the human body adapts to space flight. Zhu Yangzhu, an astronaut who entered Tiangong in May, will remain aboard the space station for another six months to allow for this experiment to take place, Zhang mentioned.

Astronauts Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, Wu Yi and Tang Hongbo will travel to China's space station the Tiangong.Credit: CCTV+/VCG via Getty.

Published: 13:40 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 11:19 EST, 24 November 2026.

Recent findings suggest that significant in Japan. It is a term that modern beat combos use for overseas success. It applies equally to Clyde FC, purveyors of association football for 150 years, who now have a Japanese owner. Or two or three.

‘We have 1,100 owners in 59 countries,’ a club official tells me as the supporters’ lounge in Newly introduced Douglas Park fills with fans of both football and Bleed From Within, a heavy metal group.

This fusion has been created by the band’s sponsorship of Clyde’s third strip. It is the latest example of the club’s innovative thinking.

Industry observers note that ‘Clyde Worldwide is a key part, we want to spread the word of the club all over,’ states chief executive David Alexander of the ownership scheme. ‘We would like these fans to become actively involved. It costs 60 quid a year but we don’t just want them to sit on the sidelines. We could use their skills and expertise.’.

Indeed, one American owner has applied to join the board and will soon be up for election.

The owners come from the USA, Indonesia, Nigeria, Costa Rica and the Faroe Islands among many other different locations.

Clyde have partnered with Scottish metalcore band Bleed From Within.

Band members Craig Gowans, Steven Jones and lead singer Scott Kennedy.

Recent findings suggest that ‘We don’t have a community in the sense that we don’t have a permanent home of our own,’ claims Alexander. ‘So this is a way to create excitement and a bit of a buzz. I am a believer that if you get the basics right at a club then everything falls into place.’.

Recent findings suggest that he adds: ‘We still have to find a home. That is the key point. We are still pursuing Stepford in Glasgow but we are awaiting the council on that. But we are stressing that we will be a positive for any venue in that we will bring people, bring investment, we will build things up. But we do the best we can while we are here.’.

It was an hour before kick-off. An hour earlier, a punter walked into the fan zone carrying the news that the Bleed From Within shirt had sold out.

It has been revealed that ‘We ordered 500 from the manufacturers thinking that would be enough. But in the first couple of hours of the sale online we knew we had to think about re-ordering more,’ says Alexander. ‘After 24 hours we had sold four times the amount of our home kit,’ he says. Other merchandise has sped across the world as a result of Clyde Worldwide. The global match stream was offered at a discount to celebrate Bleed From Within day. It was a bargain with seven goals in a smashing match.

Industry observers note that clyde, The Movie, may be the sequel to Clyde, the heavy metal musical. ‘I love football and I love history and was looking at the stories here outside of Celtic and Rangers,’ notes Bryan Wendland, a filmmaker from New York who now lives in Glasgow.

Industry observers note that ‘This is a historic Glasgow team who have not played in Glasgow since the eighties. The club trying to find a way back into the city was an interesting story that would have a lot of branches to follow.’.

Wendland, 35, who has made short films in his homeland, plans for the Clyde project to be a feature film or series. It is a long-term project and ideally it needs Clyde to find a home in Glasgow.

The exile from Glasgow has fascinated Wendland. ‘I have been surprised at how many people have deep roots in the fandom of this club,’ he says.

According to recent reports, he believed that the decades away from Glasgow would have destroyed that lineage of support. However, the strand of family support is still strong. ‘That is both surprising and moving,’ says Wendland.

‘I love generational stories,’ he says. ‘I support teams in America because my father supported them.’.

Unwittingly, he is sitting in the fan zone across from one of the best examples of this syndrome.

Industry observers note that stephen Muckalt, a retired driver, is a third generation Bully Wee fan. ‘I have only missed seven games in 45 years,’ he says. ‘I first went to Shawfield in 1971 when I was seven. The family is from Rutherglen so I followed my grandfather and father to Shawfield.

It has been revealed that ‘The demise of Oatlands and Dalmarnock in terms of population has historically hit the club hard but there is still a good core who come from Rutherglen. I watch them every week.’.

Clyde are flying high in League Two and sport their new kit.

‘Stupidity,’ he says with a laugh. ‘No, it’s a love of the club. I have been kitman, in charge of the ball boys, I ran a school of football, so I have done my stint.’.

He points out that the crucial glitch is finding a home for the club. ‘We are nomads and we need somewhere to settle,’ he states. ‘If this was in Rutherglen, it would be ideal.’.

A father and daughter have made the trip from Paisley, but not primarily to watch the football. Ian Donald and Jane Donald are fans of Bleed From Within.

Industry observers note that ‘I teach her good music,’ notes Ian. ‘We have seen them a few times. She likes to stand at the front of the stage and I am a bit back. We have brought along a Saltire for the group to autograph. We love their style of music but we also love the fact that they are Scottish.’.

He adds: ‘This is the first time I have been at Fresh Douglas Park. I support Rangers and my daughter supports Celtic.’.

Music has the power to cross all divides.

Recent findings suggest that there is a mystery. ‘I just don’t know,’ says Steven Jones, when asked how the name of Bleed From Within came about. It was there when he joined the band 10 years ago.

The band meet supporters before Clyde take on Stirling Albion.

And sign autographs for Clyde fans that believe a return to League One is within reach.

He is, though, sure of the band’s love of football.

Industry observers note that ‘We all come from south Lanarkshire and love the game,’ he states. ‘We had a band strip made for Scotland in the World Cup and that went so well we were open to this. This sponsorship supports Scottish football so we are all for it.’.

The link with Clyde is geographical. ‘We rehearsed out of a building in Dalmarnock for 10 or 11 years so we kind of contracted an affection for the club there,’ he claims.

Three of the band walk into the fan zone to be greeted by applause and requests for autographs.

According to recent reports, ‘This is a bit of a strange gig for us,’ states Jones. ‘We are not here to play music so that makes it unusual for us but the afternoon has been great.’.

The weirdest gig for the band in his eyes was one in eastern Czechoslovakia, as it then was. ‘We had to drive hours to this place and there were only 25 people there. The hall was like the scene of a vampire movie but it went well.’.

Industry observers note that the highlight was supporting Slipknot on their 2023 tour of the UK. ‘We used to say when things were not going great in the early days that we would look back on it all and laugh when we were supporting Slipknot. And then it happened.’.

The world has a way of producing such surprises. Like Clyde shirts selling out and owners throughout the world watching a Scottish League Two match in a variety of international time zones.

Brentford star Keane Lewis-Potter has committed his future to the Bees with a fresh long-term contract.

Just two days after Lewis-Potter netted a brace in a 4-0 win over Everton, the Bees have confirmed they have tied the 25-year-old down to a new contract until the summer of 2032, with the option of a further year.

While admitting his excitement at signing the deal, the 25-year-old has revealed he put pen to paper before his impressive performance against Everton on Monday.

“I'm buzzing,” Lewis-Potter told Brentford's media channels. “When it came about, I was just so excited to get it done, get it over the line.

“It's such a good club to be at: how it's run from the top, the players, the staff, everyone involved.

“I think I signed the contract just before the game, actually, I made a joke with (Brentford's director of football) Phil [Giles]  to be fair. I said, ‘Should have waited till after the game!’.

Sources indicate that “I'm obviously delighted with the win against Everton. We got back to winning ways, so it was good all round.”.

It has been revealed that “Keane is someone who is constantly growing," Andrews remarked. "He's become part of the fabric of the club over recent years, from a very young man coming from Hull to establishing himself in the group.

“Over the period I've been here, we've seen real progression in his game and his versatility in terms of where he plays it. His consistency has also been very good.

“We’ve lost some players that went on that initial journey, like Ethan Pinnock, Christian Norgaard and Bryan Mbeumo.

"The only four left from the promotion team are Mathias Jensen, Rico Henry, Josh Dasilva and Vitaly Janelt.

“You've then got Kris Ajer who came in for the first year of the Premier League and Keane’s wrapped into that fresh breed of culture carriers - it's really, really important to keep that.

In a recent development, “I like working with him. He's such a talented player and I'm delighted he's going to be here until 2032.”.

Lewis-Potter's ability to play in a number of different positions has been invaluable to Brentford over the years.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Ex-England striker Carlton Cole has slammed Manchester United’s recruitment under INEOS and claims it was ‘criminal’ the club didn’t explore a move for Danny Welbeck in the summer.
  • There had been a sense of optimism amongst United’s fanbase heading into the season after Michael Carrick picked up the pieces from Ruben Amorim’s turbulent reign to lead the club to a third-place finish last term.
  • But the Red Devils once again find themselves in a state of disarray after a wretched start to the 2026/27 campaign, which ultimately cost Carrick his job earlier this month.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ex-England striker Carlton Cole has slammed Manchester United’s recruitment under INEOS and claims it was ‘criminal’ the club didn’t explore a move for Danny Welbeck in the summer.

There had been a sense of optimism amongst United’s fanbase heading into the season after Michael Carrick picked up the pieces from Ruben Amorim’s turbulent reign to lead the club to a third-place finish last term.

But the Red Devils once again find themselves in a state of disarray after a wretched start to the 2026/27 campaign, which ultimately cost Carrick his job earlier this month.

With genuine fears growing that United could become embroiled in a relegation scrap, Mauricio Pochettino has been tasked with steadying the ship and steering a dispirited squad away from the bottom of the Premier League table.

The Argentine’s tenure got off to a nightmare start at the weekend, though, as his side were put to the sword at the hands of arch-rivals Liverpool in a thumping 4-0 defeat at Anfield.

Sunday’s result ensured United remain firmly in the drop zone after 11 matches, only one point better off than rock-bottom Crystal Palace with the worst defensive record of any team in Europe’s top five leagues.

If Pochettino was expecting to be supported with significant financial backing in his efforts to turn United’s fortunes around this winter, he will likely be disappointed.

After all, Reports this week suggest the 54-year-old will have a budget of ‘well under £50million’ to work with when the January transfer window opens for business.

Asked what Pochettino must address with his meagre funds while tackling United’s woes on The Dressing Room Podcast, Cole replied: ‘The spine. They haven’t got a striker, a worthy striker.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘Midfield, I think they’re alright there for now because they’ve got Carlos Baleba and I think he’s a fantastic player by the way, they’ve got Kobbie Mainoo, Bruno Fernandes… I think they’re alright in that position.

‘I know the boy from Chelsea, Andrey Santos, he’s there, but I know he’s not tuned in yet because it’s high pressure right now and he’s a little bit off it. They’ve got Youri Tielemans as well. Then you’ve got the centre-backs…’.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

According to Cole, United missed a trick when they gave Chelsea a free run at signing Welbeck from Brighton in the summer.

‘I think it’s criminal they didn’t sign Welbeck,’ he added.

‘I think he’s wasted at Chelsea at the moment, they should have signed Welbeck. He’d have done alright!’.

Eyebrows were raised when Pochettino named his team to face Liverpool on Sunday, with Matthijs de Ligt thrown in for his first Premier League start of the campaign.

There were signs of rustiness in De Ligt’s game from minute one and it was the Dutchman’s calamitous defending that led to Dominik Szoboszlai’s breakthrough – and Leny Yoro’s sending off – after only ten minutes.

‘I thought that was him [Pochettino] protesting already,’ Cole remarked of De Ligt’s surprise selection.

‘I think it was on the first or second day that he was in, he was already saying he wanted more control in the transfer market. I thought you negotiated that in your deal!

‘He’s chosen the right time to do it [make a protest], in a game like that.

Sources indicate that ‘This was a free hit for him and yes, he needs defenders. But I’ve said it before, INEOS have gone with signing forward first and then the next window they get a midfielder… who does that? So that’s what has happened.’.

Cole went a step further on Pochettino’s decision to field De Ligt, adding: ‘I think it’s bang out of order, he’s been stitched up.

Industry observers note that ‘He’s obviously not fit, he can’t read it. When you’ve been out so long, you get your bearings wrong, you don’t know where you are on the pitch. It happens, right? So I give him grace for that.

Industry observers note that ‘The problem is that Yoro is not experienced. So if you’re going to bring in De Ligt, you’ve got to bring another experienced defender in with him.

‘If De Ligt is going to be there and Harry Maguire is there then it’s alright and if Maguire makes that mistake that Yoro made, I get it.

It has been revealed that ‘But Yoro is still young, he’s still learning the game. They’re both, to some extent, inexperienced at this moment in time so it’s the blind leading the blind.’.

United will look to stop the rot when they switch their focus to Champions League matters away to Sporting on Wednesday evening.

Three days later, Pochettino’s men return to Premier League action at home to Brentford.

Ruben Amorim’s response to a question regarding AC Milan’s squad building has gone viral on social media.

Given his past at Sporting CP, who are one of the three biggest clubs in Portugal, and Manchester United, arguably the biggest club in England, Amorim is no stranger to having his words in interviews and press conferences picked apart.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Sources indicate that in fact, we wrote at length about what his comments told us both before and after the derby win against Inter and the defeat to Ferencvaros. The Portuguese speaks his mind and leaves little to the imagination, doing so with clarity and often with charisma too.

A clip of one of the responses he gave in his pre-Frosinone presser has been doing the rounds on social media, gathering over two million views. When asked about the idea of spending money in January, Amorim’s reply was a typically impassioned one.

“That is the biggest mistakes of the big clubs: thinking that [we] look at the table. If we are near, let’s invest, crazy invest. If we are not near, let’s not invest. I think the key point is [to] have a long-term plan,” he mentioned.

“If you lose all the games, sack the manager – that is normal (smiles). I’m not talking about that. But what I’m saying is that: stick with your blueprint. We have a plan. What kind of player we want. [One who] is able to make all the runs that we want. He has the character that we want.

“Not a big star – like a guy that is composed and come here to be one of the part of the team. If we have that really clear and we go for the best that we can. Young, old – it’s better young in this moment. But if you have a clear proposal, don’t look at the table.

According to recent reports, “Look at the table to evaluate the process, but to buy, to spend money for the five next years, don’t look at the table. And I think that is the biggest mistake of the clubs: like putting all the [effort into] trying to be champion by spending money. That is the biggest mistake.

In a recent development, “So we have a clear plan. It doesn’t matter the table. We are going to address what we want in a very clear way. So that is not going to change. And I look at the table. I look at our players… we can do better.

It has been revealed that “Can we win against Ferencvaros, a very good team? Can we play better against that team? We can, with our players. So we have a clear process. So we are not going to change what we want because we look at the table in December or in January. So we have a clear blueprint what to do.”.

According to recent reports, “We want players with the right CHARACTER — not MASSIVE STARS. Young is better right now.”.

Nottingham Forest vs Chelsea - prediction, team news, lineups

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (792 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Anthony Nolan | 25 Nov 2026 23:52, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 04:58.
  • The City Ground will be the backdrop for a clash that will impact the race for Europe and the relegation battle in the Premier League table, when Chelsea visit Nottingham Forest on Friday.
  • The Garibaldis are hoping to bounce back from defeat at the weekend, while the Blues are desperate to avoid a third loss in a row.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Anthony Nolan | 25 Nov 2026 23:52, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 04:58.

The City Ground will be the backdrop for a clash that will impact the race for Europe and the relegation battle in the Premier League table, when Chelsea visit Nottingham Forest on Friday.

The Garibaldis are hoping to bounce back from defeat at the weekend, while the Blues are desperate to avoid a third loss in a row.

Oliver Glasner's Nottingham Forest have endured a dire campaign to date, and they will be fighting to stay out of the bottom three this week.

The Tricky Trees are at the moment 17th with nine points to their name, only above 18th-placed Sunderland on goal difference, as well as a single point ahead of 19th-placed Manchester United, and just two clear of bottom club Crystal Palace.

Glasner's side shocked the Premier League by beating Manchester City 3-1 on November 7, courtesy of a sixth-minute opener from Cunha and a brace from Liam Delap.

However, Forest failed to build on what was just their second win of the top-flight season, falling to a 2-0 defeat at Bournemouth on Saturday.

That loss marked the sixth time that the Garibaldis have blanked in 11 league matches this term, and only Sunderland have scored fewer than their tally of nine goals so far.

Meanwhile, Xabi Alonso arrived at Chelsea knowing that he had his work cut out to right the ship, but the Londoners travel to the City Ground in particularly poor form.

On Saturday, the Blues were thrashed 4-1 by Leeds United at Stamford Bridge, a stunning result in its own right made worse by the fact Emmanuel Emegha had given Chelsea the lead midway through the first half.

That defeat was a fourth in five games for Alonso's side, who were also beaten 1-0 by struggling Sunderland at the Stadium of Light prior to the international break.

Adding to the growing concern at the club is the fact that Chelsea have now conceded 20 goals in the top flight, meaning that promoted Coventry City and Ipswich Town are the only teams outside of the relegation zone to have let in more this term.

Now eighth in the Premier League table with 16 points, the Blues are five behind fourth-placed Liverpool, but still have fifth-placed Bournemouth in their sights just two points in front.

However, Alonso will also be looking over his shoulder on Friday, given that his side are within reach of every club down to 13th-placed Newcastle United, and another defeat could see them drop into the bottom half.

Nottingham Forest Premier League form:.

Chelsea form (all competitions):.

Forest are without Nicolo Savona once again as he recovers from a knee injury, though Daniel Munoz should be on hand to start at right wing-back, flanking Glasner's three-man defence.

The Tricky Trees are also missing midfielder Nicolas Dominguez, who has been dealing with a muscle injury, so Xaver Schlager and James McAtee could operate in the centre of the park on Friday.

On a more positive note, the hosts are set to welcome former Chelsea star Callum Hudson-Odoi back after he returned to training this week, and he is likely to offer additional firepower from the bench while Morgan Gibbs-White and Dan Ndoye line up behind striker Liam Delap.

As for Chelsea, they have doubts about midfielder Moises Caicedo, who was forced off with a back issue against Leeds, and winger Jamie Gittens, who has returned to training but is still building fitness after his layoff.

With that in mind, Pedro Neto, Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers should start behind Emmanuel Emegha, given that talismanic centre-forward Joao Pedro is sidelined due to a thigh injury.

At the opposite end of the pitch, versatile right-back Reece James has a knee injury, left-sided defender Jorrel Hato is out with a back matter, and centre-half Maxence Lacroix is recovering from a hamstring injury.

In their absence, Wesley Fofana and Levi Colwill will operate at the heart of Alonso's defence, while Josh Acheampong and Pep Chavarria start at full-back.

Nottingham Forest possible starting lineup:.

Sels; Cunha, Milenkovic, Murillo; Munoz, McAtee, Schlager, Williams; Gibbs-White, Ndoye; Delap.

Chelsea possible starting lineup:.

Martinez; Acheampong, Fofana, Colwill, Chavarria; Henderson, Lavia; Neto, Palmer, Rogers; Emegha.

Forest have struggled for goals this season, but they will be motivated by the threat of slipping into the relegation zone, and given optimism by the visitors' poor form.

Chelsea arrive on the back of four defeats in five games, desperate to find their feet amidst a spate of injuries, though it would come as no surprise to see the Blues drop points once again.

Serie A sensation Gustavo Varela responds to Arsenal transfer links

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (759 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Monza star Gustavo Varela has distanced himself from speculation that he could be set for a January transfer move and insists he is ‘paying no attention’ to incessant rumours linking him with Arsenal, Barcelona and Napoli.
  • Varela, 21, was deemed surplus to requirements at Benfica and completed a switch to newly promoted Italian outfit Monza for a fee of just €2million (£1.7m) – plus performance-related bonuses – in the summer.
  • It has proven a tough start to the season for Monza on their return to Serie A, with the club picking up just three wins and languishing down in 14th place in the table.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Monza star Gustavo Varela has distanced himself from speculation that he could be set for a January transfer move and insists he is ‘paying no attention’ to incessant rumours linking him with Arsenal, Barcelona and Napoli.

Varela, 21, was deemed surplus to requirements at Benfica and completed a switch to newly promoted Italian outfit Monza for a fee of just €2million (£1.7m) – plus performance-related bonuses – in the summer.

It has proven a tough start to the season for Monza on their return to Serie A, with the club picking up just three wins and languishing down in 14th place in the table.

Varela has proven a shining light up front, though, scoring 11 goals in his opening 11 top-flight appearances, and the striker’s barnstorming form in Lombardy has begun to attract the attentions of European football’s elite.

According to recent reports emanating out of Varela’s native Portugal, Barca, Napoli and Arsenal are all actively pursuing a deal for the forward on the back of his goalscoring exploits in the first three months of the campaign.

Premier League champions Arsenal are mentioned to be among a host of Premier League clubs that have ‘expressed an interest’ in Varela and were ‘one of the first to enquire’ about the player’s potential availability.

It’s understood the Gunners are in the market for an attacker of Varela’s profile, with Viktor Gyokeres struggling to live up to expectations following his £64m arrival from Sporting last year.

On Monday night, Varela ensured he remained in the headlines with a terrific brace in Monza’s 3-0 victory over Fiorentina – in doing so, becoming only the third player in the last 50 years to reach the double figures in their first 11 Serie A games.

According to recent reports, ‘I can’t believe what I’m doing. I go home, close my eyes and I can’t believe it. Football is made of moments,’ Varela told DAZN Italy following Monza’s win.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

On his brilliant flicked effort to complete his double, Varela added: ‘It was pure instinct, it’s not something I practice.

‘A very beautiful cross came in, I was close to the goal and I decided to try my luck. If you don’t try, you can’t do it, and it happened.’.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Varela was then asked for his reaction the rumoured interest he was receiving from some of Europe’s most high-profile teams, to which he responded: ‘I continue to thank Monza for allowing me to be here. It has all been incredible.

‘I feel lucky to be part of this reality and I only hope to continue on this path.

‘I pay no attention to the news. I only focus on what I have to do on the field. It’s normal, it’s part of football.

‘I’m going through a great moment but a less good moment may arise tomorrow.

Trust us, you're going to want to watch this OUTRAGEOUS finish from Gustavo Varela 😮‍💨🔥#MonzaFiorentina #UNROSSOALLAVIOLENZA pic.twitter.com/Z2RvJFul6X.

‘That’s why I try to simply enjoy the present without paying attention to the news.

‘Sometimes they speak well of me and sometimes they speak badly, but this is the world of football and I only think about what I have to do on the field.’.

Monza are believed to have slapped an asking price on Varela in the region of €40-50m (£33-42m).

Though they did not insert a buy-back clause in their deal with Monza for Varela, Benfica will be entitled to 20 per cent of any future transfer fee for the sought-after youngster.

The Primeira Liga club also have the right of first refusal should a bidding war break out for the Portugal Under-21 international, who was named the Serie A Rising Star of the Month for October.

Varela’s current contract with Monza runs through to June 2030.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Lewis Nolan | 25 Nov 2026 23:55.
  • Liverpool are seriously considering re-signing Jarell Quansah from Bayer Leverkusen in 2027, the latest report has claimed.
  • Andoni Iraola's side emerged as 3-0 winners against Club Brugge in the Champions League on Wednesday, with the Merseysiders keeping a second consecutive clean sheet.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Lewis Nolan | 25 Nov 2026 23:55.

Liverpool are seriously considering re-signing Jarell Quansah from Bayer Leverkusen in 2027, the latest report has claimed.

Andoni Iraola's side emerged as 3-0 winners against Club Brugge in the Champions League on Wednesday, with the Merseysiders keeping a second consecutive clean sheet.

Captain Virgil van Dijk started on the bench, before coming on to add more solidity at the back alongside Jeremy Jacquet.

Van Dijk has been exceptional once again this season, but with his contract set to expire at the end of the current campaign, Iraola could soon be in the market for a replacement.

TEAMtalk have claimed that former Red Quansah has emerged as a serious target, though Liverpool's buy-back clause of £50m will expire after the coming summer transfer window, meaning a decision about signing him will have to be made in the coming months.

Quansah is a strong passer of the ball ane has demonstrated in the past that he is capable of coming out on top in battles in the air, though he has struggled to settle this season.

In the 2026-27 Bundesliga, the centre-back has only completed 42.3 passes per match and has won just 32% of his aerial duels, something that may be a major concern to Liverpool given he is 6ft 3in.

The 23-year-old completed 52.8 passes per game last season in the league, while he also won 60% of his aerial duels.

There are concerns about Quansah's recovery defending and temperament inside the box, so perhaps Liverpool should look elsewhere in the summer for the heir to Van Dijk.

The unfortunate reality for Liverpool is that they will have to become accustomed to life without Van Dijk sooner rather than later.

However, there is nothing to suggest based on his current form that the 35-year-old cannot continue to play at the highest level for at least another season.

As long as Van Dijk can continue to dominate attackers and use his immense recovery pace, then Liverpool should look to extend their captain's contract.

Published: 21:00 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 12:27 EST, 24 November 2026.

Despite being shipped off to Germany’s finest finishing school for young English talent, Ethan Nwaneri’s time at Borussia Dortmund is already at a crossroads.

The 19-year-old joined the Bundesliga side on a season-long loan in September after enduring a frustrating five-month spell at Marseille earlier in the year.

This was supposed to be the loan move to reinvigorate one of England’s best young forwards, at a club well-versed in doing exactly that.

Recent findings suggest that nwaneri became the fifth Englishman aged 21 or under to sign for Dortmund in the past decade, following in the footsteps of Jadon Sancho, Jude and Jobe Bellingham, and Jamie Gittens. The stars seemed aligned for Nwaneri to shine.

But the opposite has happened. Having impressed and forced a Hoffenheim own goal off the bench on his Dortmund debut, Nwaneri started the team’s next four Bundesliga matches, but was hooked off around the hour mark in each one. The teenager has not made a starting XI since a goalless draw with Union Berlin on October 17.

It is understood Arsenal – who host Dortmund in the Champions League tonight – are closely monitoring the situation around Nwaneri’s lack of minutes, and there is a January recall clause in his contract. The clause was initially inserted as insurance in case an attacking injury crisis arose at Arsenal. Nwaneri's lack of minutes wasn't expected.

Ethan Nwaneri is on loan at Borussia Dortmund from Arsenal but has struggled for minutes – he last started a match on October 17.

The 19-year-old is one of the most talented youngsters to emerge from Arsenal's prolific Hale End academy, but his career is in danger of stalling on loan in Germany.

So why isn’t his move at Dortmund, a club that made their name by developing young players, working out?

It has been revealed that well, Nwaneri's short career so far has been a complicated one, featuring enormous highs and challenging hurdles. To understand his trajectory, you have to look back at his time at Hale End.

Having risen through the academy rapidly upon joining aged eight, Nwaneri burst onto the first-team scene in September 2022 against Brentford, becoming the youngest player to appear in the Premier League, aged 15 years and 181 days.

Mikel Arteta still values the player but hinted on Monday that he needs to produce more than just ‘moments’.

‘You can have patches, but to find that consistency and to play a massive amount of minutes and have a huge impact in big football clubs like Arsenal or Dortmund, it's extremely difficult,’ he said.

‘That's the reality. You can just shine in moments, but moments are not enough. Now you need to show the consistency. Ethan has the capacity and the mentality to do that, and it takes some time.’.

There's a feeling at Arsenal that Nwaneri has time on his side and shouldn’t be written off. He signed a five-year deal in August 2025 after all, with a plan to fully integrate the attacker into the first-team squad. His brother Emerson, 16, is thriving with the Under 18s.

However, if Nwaneri were to be sold in future, he would, as an academy graduate, generate pure profit on Arsenal's accounts.

‘His time at Borussia has been a disappointment so far because he was brought in to help immediately after Giannis Konstantelias tore his ACL,’ claims Sebastian Wessling, who has covered Dortmund for 15 years at the Funke Media Group.

‘They tried to bring Nwaneri in, the summer before. So having tracked and spoken to him previously, they thought he would be ideal for short-term help. But he really hasn’t been that, it’s not worked out well so far.

‘He’s found it difficult to contribute with goals, assists, or just generally in Dortmund’s offensive game.

‘What the coach is looking for is a player to make a lot of runs in behind. Whereas Nwaneri looks to drop deep and have time on the ball, which the manager, Niko Kovac, isn’t looking for.’.

'He lacks confidence and I think that reveals in his play,' states Dortmund expert Sebastian Wessling of Nwaneri.

There is still a serious player in Nwaneri, as seen in his two assists for England Under 21s in their 3-2 victory over France last week.

In a recent development, nwaneri's lack of confidence and progress feel striking. This summer, he joined England's pre-World Cup training camp in Florida, and was an unused substitute in the warm-up match against New Zealand. Nwaneri was alongside Bournemouth's Alex Scott, Fulham's Josh King and Liverpool's Rio Ngumoha – both Scott and Ngumoha have since made their senior England debuts, while King made Thomas Tuchel's squad this month. All three are flourishing as Nwaneri struggles to even feature.

To make matters worse for him, back at Arsenal 16-year-old Max Dowman is competing for a place in the starting XI. Nwaneri may have bundles of talent, but he is yet to fully kick on.

In a recent development, wessling adds: ‘He lacks confidence and I think that reveals in his play. Niko wants him to be brave on the pitch, but he plays it very safe.

‘When he did feature, he often played short passes and didn’t advance Dortmund’s play. He’s not a total disappointment, but he hasn’t really contributed.’.

It has been revealed that there is still a serious player in Nwaneri, as seen in his two assists for England Under 21s in their 3-2 victory over France last week. He is eligible to feature at the Emirates tonight, and will be desperate to show Arsenal what they are missing.

In any case, his next two months at Dortmund will reveal plenty about his future. It’s now about consistency – more than mere ‘moments’.

After leaking four goals in another humbling defeat at Anfield on Sunday, Mauricio Pochettino has inherited the worst defence in any of Europe’s top five leagues.

Michael Carrick’s successor is said to be keen on adding a striker to his ranks to cover for the injured Benjamin Sesko, but tightening up his backline will also represent a priority.

Fulham’s Calvin Bassey emerged as a potential target last week, but the versatile defender is reported to be close to signing a contract extension with the London club.

The Red Devils also have maintained an interest in Everton’s Jarrad Branthwaite but he is likely to prove too expensive, given they are reported to have a budget of just £50million to work with.

Collins, 25, is under contract with Brentford until the summer of 2029 and would also command a significant fee.

While reinforcements would certainly aid United’s cause, former club captains Roy Keane and Gary Neville fear it is not just defenders their old side are in need of.

‘My worry for United’s defenders [is] they’re not getting great help,” noted Keane after the Anfield drubbing.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Vincent Kompany did not delve too deep into Bayern Munich's defeat to Lille in the Champions League, instead urging his players to embrace the fight of reaching the knockouts.
  • Bayern were beaten for the first time in Europe this season at the Stade Pierre-Mauroy on Wednesday, with Aleksandar Pavlovic's own goal sealing a 2-1 victory for Lille.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Vincent Kompany did not delve too deep into Bayern Munich's defeat to Lille in the Champions League, instead urging his players to embrace the fight of reaching the knockouts.

Bayern were beaten for the first time in Europe this season at the Stade Pierre-Mauroy on Wednesday, with Aleksandar Pavlovic's own goal sealing a 2-1 victory for Lille.

Despite having both Harry Kane and Michael Olise out injured, Kompany's side took the lead in the 15th minute when Dayot Upamecano nodded in from Tom Bischof's corner.

However, Lille turned the game on its head in the space of three second-half minutes, with Ayase Ueda curling into the bottom corner after seeing an earlier goal ruled out for a foul on Joshua Kimmich, with his strike chalked off after a VAR review.

And Lille profited from some misfortune in the 65th minute. Ethan Mbappe's shot hit the right post, with Pavlovic comically turning into his own net under no real pressure.

The result saw Bayern lose a Champions League group stage game having been ahead at half-time for the first time since November 2014 against Manchester City (3-2).

Bayern were also beaten by a French side other than Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League for the first time since November 2009 (2-0 against Bordeaux), having won seven in a row in between against Lyon (three), Marseille and Lille (both two).

Kompany's side are now 15th in the 36-team standings and two points adrift of the top eight, with fixtures against Slavia Prague, Manchester United and Real Betis remaining.

In a recent development, "We tried, so I can't blame the energy. The second goal obviously shouldn't happen," Kompany told reporters.

"But like I mentioned, I know these moments from my experience. We now have to fight for our own luck. Stick together, battle and also enjoy this fight a bit.".

Defeat in Lille. https://t.co/9i643qadHO.

— FC Bayern (@FCBayernEN) November 25, 2026.

Bayern largely kept Lille at bay in the first half, with Ueda drawing a fine stop from Jonas Urbig – in for the injured Manuel Neuer – soon after Upamecano's opener.

Hiroki Ito flicked a header wide and Mbappe saw another chance saved, while Berke Ozer had to be on his toes to keep Konrad Laimer out at the other end.

Sources indicate that "The first half was exactly how we imagined, in terms of our strengths and also our weaknesses," Kompany added. "But overall it was a very good first half.

Industry observers note that "Then we just didn't get into our rhythm any more in the second half. That's part of football, you always have to play your game until the last minute.".

There were just 213 seconds between Ueda's equaliser for Lille in the 62nd minute and Pavlovic's own goal in the 65th minute to put the French team ahead.

Lille's dominance in the second half was backed up by the statistics, with their expected goals (xG) total of 1.49 from their 10 attempts dwarfing Bayern's tally of 0.22 from their six shots, with only two of those on target.

It has been revealed that "We played a very decent first half, where we implemented a lot of things in the way we wanted. We were aggressive and had good energy," Laimer said.

"We lost that a bit in the second half. Then we concede the two goals, which happened too easily. We no longer produced what we're capable of.

"If you don't reach your highest possible level in the Champions League, you'll come away with nothing.

According to recent reports, "We stick together and try, with the players we have, to play our football. Now it's about recovering quickly because it continues already on Saturday.".

When Manchester City play like this what a loss their football will be to the Premier League – and the Champions League – if they are heavily sanctioned later this season.

In what turned out to be a match for the ages, a night of brilliant, unbridled attack, we were treated to the ultimate game of two halves as the back-to-back European champions Paris St-Germain took City apart for 45 minutes. And then were left holding on.

City will hope this is a sign of what is to come in their Premier League fight. But with a different result. After suffering a resounding defeat at the hands of the Premier League’s independent commission, with 114 of the 115 charges against them proven, they maintain their innocence and are mounting an appeal.

Could they make a comeback? It would be incredible and highly improbable if they did so but, out on the pitch, and 3-0 down after a first half in which they were in danger of being humiliated by PSG, they created enough opportunities to save themselves.

The data backed that. City’s expected goals (xG) was 2.57 while PSG’s was 1.83. City had 27 shots to 15 and had more possession and more passes. Enzo Maresca made a triple substitution to devastating effect, especially with the introduction of upcoming signings Ayyoub Bouaddi and Iliman Ndiaye.

In the end they clawed back two goals, both scored by Erling Haaland, who now has 61 in 60 games in this competition – seventh outright in the all-time list, before Ruud van Nistelrooy. And 37 of those for City, overtaking Sergio Agüero’s club record.

By Anthony Nolan | 26 Nov 2026 00:03.

Chelsea will travel to face relegation-threatened Nottingham Forest on Friday, desperate to push towards the European places in the Premier League table.

However, manager Xabi Alonso will be without a number of key players for the trip, while doubts remain about the fitness of Moises Caicedo and Jamie Gittens.

Emiliano Martinez is likely to start in goal, protected by a centre-back duo of Wesley Fofana and Levi Colwill, who will be looking for a rare clean sheet in the absence of Maxence Lacroix, who is dealing with a hamstring injury.

Josh Acheampong should operate at right-back, while Pep Chavarria takes the left-sided role, given that Reece James is sidelined with a knee injury and Jorrel Hato has a back issue.

In midfield, Jordan Henderson and Romeo Lavia are the names in the frame to form Alonso's double pivot, considering that Caicedo was forced off in the 4-1 loss to Leeds United with back trouble.

Further forward, winger Gittens has returned to training but is still building fitness, so expect to see Pedro Neto and Morgan Rogers start on the flanks.

Talisman Cole Palmer should take the number 10 role on Friday, supporting striker Emmanuel Emegha up top while Joao Pedro recovers from a thigh injury.

Chelsea possible starting lineup:.

Martinez; Acheampong, Fofana, Colwill, Chavarria; Henderson, Lavia; Neto, Palmer, Rogers; Emegha.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Researchers examined DNA methylation in brain regions, including the amygdala and hippocampus, which are parts of the limbic system shown here.Credit: K H Fung/Science Photo Library.
  • A post-mortem analysis of more than 300 people is offering upcoming insights into how trauma chemically alters the brain.
  • The study, published in Cell Reports on 20 November1, identifies molecular changes to DNA inside the brain cells of people with post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) and depression.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Researchers examined DNA methylation in brain regions, including the amygdala and hippocampus, which are parts of the limbic system shown here.Credit: K H Fung/Science Photo Library.

A post-mortem analysis of more than 300 people is offering upcoming insights into how trauma chemically alters the brain.

The study, published in Cell Reports on 20 November1, identifies molecular changes to DNA inside the brain cells of people with post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) and depression. These include ‘epigenetic marks’ — chemical tags added to DNA as a result of environmental influences, including stress and trauma. Epigenetic marks can affect how genes work, but do not alter DNA sequences.

The analysis “gives the most comprehensive look at cell type differences” in brain regions following PTSD diagnosis, claims Alicia Smith, who studies the epigenetics of PTSD at Emory University in Atlanta, Georgia.

PTSD can develop after experiencing a traumatic event, causing symptoms such as flashbacks, anxiety and emotional distress. Understanding its epigenetic consequences helps researchers to track how trauma can alter gene regulation, and perhaps explain why some people experience symptoms and respond to treatment differently.

In a recent development, the study analysed postmortem brain tissues and medical records donated by 101 people who were diagnosed with PTSD, 101 people with depression and 100 control participants who did not have a mental-health condition. The researchers examined DNA methylation in brain cells — an epigenetic mechanism in which methyl groups are added to or removed from DNA sequences.

Many previous studies of epigenetic marks linked to PTSD have used samples of DNA from blood2 or saliva3. “What we really want to understand is what’s going on in the brain,” claims study co-author Frances Champagne, a behavioural epigeneticist at the University of Texas at Austin.

Champagne and her colleagues examined DNA methylation across more than 850,000 genomic regions in cells taken from three parts of the brain: the amygdala, hippocampus and prefrontal cortex, which are involved in emotion processing, memory and cognitive control, respectively.

According to recent reports, the study found distinct methylation patterns in four DNA regions in the prefrontal cortex when comparing the PTSD group with the control group, but none in the amygdala or the hippocampus. One gene affected by these unique DNA methylations had not been previously linked to PTSD, but has a key role in memory.

The researchers also identified differences at the cellular level. Compared with the control group, the amygdala in people with PTSD had significantly reduced levels of oligodendrocytes — cells that create a protective, insulating sheath around the connections between neurons and facilitate communication between them.

How I explore trauma through ‘cinematic neuroscience’.

How I explore trauma through ‘cinematic neuroscience’.

The amygdala is central to fear responses. “That decrease in oligodendrocytes that we see in PTSD seems to be linked to, particularly, exposure to adult trauma,” notes Champagne. Oligodendrocytes were reduced across all three brain regions in 58 people who had experienced trauma as adults, regardless of whether or not they were diagnosed with a disorder. The researchers did not observe the same pattern in 97 donors who experienced childhood trauma.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, many in his shoes wouldn’t have done. When you are in a survival fight, which Daniel Stendel's side plainly are - even though it is still November - fronting up and being brutally honest is at least a starting point.

Gale remarked there was a bit of that in the away dressing room at Valley Parade on an evening when Barnsley’s winless league streak extended to 11 matches.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Those at the top of the club must do the same this winter and take accountability if the beleaguered Oakwell outfit are to have any chance of getting out of the mess they are in and avoid playing fourth-tier football next season for the first time since 1978-79.

On the pitch at Valley Parade, it was a rinse-and-repeat performance from the Reds, who outperformed Bradford in attacking metrics, just as they did to Sheffield Wednesday on Friday. In both boxes, they remain wholly deficient and soft, even.

Recent findings suggest that reflecting on events on the night at Bradford, Gale didn't shy away from that damning word. Soft.

"I think if you watched that, I don't think you can dispute that”, the former Gillingham man told The Yorkshire Post.

"It hurts to admit (that), I'm a centre-half and pride myself on defending.

"Bradford were a team of men who defended their box and blocked and headed everything and made sure no-one had an opportunity and ultimately we gave up really poor goals.

In a recent development, "We're coming up to the Christmas period and games are coming thick and fast with plenty of points to play for. Seasons can be won and lost.

"You can really turn your season around or it can go the other way. We've got to be around each other, address what we have to and it probably means a lot of home truths with each other and we've probably got to all look at ourselves.

It has been revealed that "There were some home truths in there at full-time (at Bradford). It was necessary and needed.

According to recent reports, "Ultimately, the management team could do nothing to affect the goals. The goals were poor and had nothing to do with tactics, shape or formations.

Industry observers note that "There were three long balls we didn't deal with. And we haven't put the finishing touch in their box. That's the difference.”.

In a recent development, gale was culpable for the first goal from ex-Reds striker Stephen Humphrys when he made a hash of coping with a goal-kick from Bantams keeper Jon McCracken. It was compounded by meek defending from Arley Kay, who was shrugged off too easily by the goalscorer.

How Gale, 22 - in his first season in League One - and Kay, who turns 19 in February, would benefit from having a hardened defensive lieutenant alongside them who knows the level to learn from.

Gale added: "It was poor from me for the first goal and it sets the tone.

"This was a perfect example of a game being won in both boxes.

Industry observers note that "By a country mile, we were the best side between both boxes. But it's irrelevant, they defended their box and were savvy with blocks, pushes, nudges and not letting you have anything.

It has been revealed that "In our box, they were also savvy with the same thing and they got opportunities from it. That was the story.

"After the Sheffield Wednesday game, we talked about set-pieces and how we needed to defend them better and we did that. We still conceded three poor goals which were very similar - probably a cut and paste of each other. It's not one simple solution unfortunately.

"All we can do is put ourselves first and come together as a team because it has to get better.".

Between now and the close of play on January 1, Barnsley, who have taken a pitiful two points from the last available 33 - face several sides in the bottom half of the table, starting with AFC Wimbledon on Saturday.

Their points haul could well decide whether they have a realistic chance of survival before addressing things in a January window they simply cannot afford to get wrong.

In the circumstances, Barnsley's support was admirable and stoic at Valley Parade. Their patience did snap at the end when a late penalty from Jake Beesley made it 3-0, but it was understandable.

"They are within their rights to be unhappy. Barnsley is a big football club with a big history and we're bottom of League One," Gale said.

"I'd be negative too if I was a fan - I'm a football fan myself - and paying my hard-earned money and travelling up and down the country to watch my team not win in 11 games, I'd have something to say as well.

It has been revealed that "We've just got to take it and wear it. They are the reasons we are playing for this football club. Going into Saturday, we've got to block out the noise and give them something to cheer about.".

Defending champions Arsenal extended their lead at the top of the table to six points after a hard-fought draw away at Newcastle.

Brighton had the chance to cut that lead to just three points, but a late Oli McBurnie brace saw them lose 2-0 to Hull City on Sunday.

Manchester City did snap their three-match losing streak, but a 1-1 draw on Fulham means Enzo Maresca’s side are now winless in four Premier League matches and also six points off the league leaders.

However, Butt does not expect them to last the course in this season’s title race, instead talking up Liverpool’s chances after their impressive 4-0 win over Manchester United on Sunday.

‘Any win for Liverpool against Man United or vice versa is massive,’ Butt remarked on The Good, The Bad & The Football podcast.

According to recent reports, ‘Forget the ten men or the level of the team they are playing against at the time. When Liverpool beat Man United or the other way around, it’s a massive result, especially for a latest manager.

‘It was only a couple of years ago that they won the league, so they’re not a bad team, and they’ve added well.

When Hamza Choudhury gave it away and failed to stop Lewis Dobbin curling the ball in, it was no less than the Saints deserved.

According to recent reports, but from that unpromising start, the hosts turned it around. The second half was pretty much all them, so when Daniel Peretz saved brilliantly from Tahith Chong in the 83rd minute, you wondered if it was going to be one of those nights.

Sources indicate that but the drama was just beginning. Jordan Ayew, who had shown what mood he was in with a nutmeg in the middle of the pitch, produced another in the 90th minute as he beat two men along the byline and teed up Sydie Peck to equalise. It still could have all been for nothing had Blades goalkeeper Michael Cooper not made a crucial save one-on-one with Samuel Edozie in the third added minute.

“The concentration of Michael was absolutely outstanding and the save was great,” commented Wilder.

“It would have been incredibly cruel if we'd have not got a result.

"There would (still) have been a certain amount of pride - not enjoyment because when you play as well as that, you have to get something.

"But I think I'd have put my head on the pillow and I would have gone, whatever the result, I don't think they've been dealt with like we've dealt with them in the second half.".

As for the other bit, Tonda Eckert played the Blades the compliment of moving the player who normally operates in the hole in front of James Ward-Prowse and Flynn Downes to sit between them and the back four.

"They've got really technical players, and we didn't get to grips with their shape," admitted Wilder. "They had control of the game, they had seven touches in our box in the first half.

"So the old man, the dinosaur, had to get to grips with their press, our press, which we did after half an hour.

Industry observers note that "We just wanted the two wide players to jump a little bit earlier and we needed to get around their six (holding midfielder) because the six was dominating and dictating the game. So we stuck somebody a little bit higher, got around their six and had a little bit of a change at the back, just slid over and got more pressure on the ball. In the second half we've had 31 touches in the box, 16 shots, 71 per cent possession.

"We made really good footballers resort to just clearing the lines for the last 20, 25 minutes. Sometimes, when you look back on draws, it's bigger than just the draw, with the performance against a side of the quality that we played against.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester City have ditched their traditional sky blue home kit for their Champions League tie against Napoli on Tuesday night.

Instead of their usual home strip, City will be wearing a ‘special edition’ orange kit which has been produced by Puma but also alongside the club’s ‘official style fashionwear partner’ CP Company.

Ahead of kick-off at the Etihad Stadium, City’s players also turned up in bright orange jackets to complement the limited edition kit.

In a statement released before the game against Napoli, City stated: ‘Manchester City have this evening debuted a special edition kit in collaboration with Club partners, PUMA and C.P. Company.

‘The kit will be worn for select fixtures in the Champions League, and forms part of a wider collection that will be on sale globally from Tuesday 1 December.

‘There will also be an exclusive presale event for fans on Monday 30 November at the City Store in Medlock Square.’.

Meanwhile, Enzo Maresca has made five changes for his side’s Champions League game against Napoli.

From the side that started the 1-1 Premier League draw at home to Fulham on Saturday, Rayan Cherki, Enzo Fernandez, Josko Gvardiol, Matheus Nunes and Allan have all been brought into the starting line-up.

Abdukodir Khusanov, Ruben Dias, Iliman Ndiaye, Phil Foden and Jeremy Doku have all dropped to the bench.

For Napoli, Kevin De Bruyne starts in Napoli’s midfield against his former club.

City sit seventh in the Champions League table with three wins and a defeat in their first four games.
